objects.definition: typedef int sock_t;
objects.description: Typedef alias defining sock_t as an int representing a socket descriptor on Unix platforms. Used wherever a socket handle is needed.

objects.definition: typedef struct stat cs_stat_t;
objects.description: Typedef alias for the system struct stat, exposing it under the portable name cs_stat_t for file status information. The actual layout is provided by the system headers and not defined here.

No custom data types are defined in this header. It only defines preprocessor macros that alias standard C allocation functions (malloc, calloc, realloc, free) under the names MG_MALLOC, MG_CALLOC, MG_REALLOC, and MG_FREE.

Lightweight string/view type describing a non-owning memory slice with pointer p and length len. Used across the API to pass strings without requiring NUL-termination. Ownership is external unless created by functions like mg_strdup/mg_strdup_nul, in which case mg_strfree should be used to release memory.

Mutable/growing byte buffer descriptor used to manage a resizable memory region (similar to a C++ string or vector<char>). Fields: buf points to the allocated storage; len is the number of valid bytes; size is the total allocated capacity (always >= len). Managed by the mbuf_* API for init, append/insert/remove, resize/trim, move, clear, and free. Construction typically via mbuf_init; must call mbuf_free to release storage. After mbuf_move, the source mbuf is emptied and the destination takes ownership of the buffer.
Built-in type; included here only if explicitly typedef’d, which it is not. No custom typedef present. Ignored.
Not defined in this header. It is referenced via includes (common/mg_str.h) and parameters/returns, but its definition is external. Per instructions, referenced-only types must be ignored.

Enumeration of logging levels used by the dbg/logging facility. LL_INFO is the default; values below/above bound markers control filtering. _LL_MIN/_LL_MAX are sentinel bounds and typically not used as actual log levels.

objects.definition: char *cs_read_file(const char *path, size_t *size);
objects.description: Function pointer type target: cs_read_file reads an entire file into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated buffer and returns a char*. Caller must free it. This entry is included only to note that no custom data types are defined; this is a function returning built-in pointer and does not define a new type. No custom struct/enum/typedef/class appears in this header.
Function pointer type target: cs_mmap_file mmaps a file and returns a char* address on platforms with CS_MMAP. This is not a custom type definition; included to clarify absence of user-defined types.

No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The only symbol present is the function declaration `int cs_hex_decode(const char *s, int len, unsigned char *dst, int *dst_len);`. Therefore, there are no types to document.

No custom types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only declares the function uint32_t cs_crc32(uint32_t crc, const void *data, uint32_t len); and includes <inttypes.h>.

objects.definition: struct cs_frbuf;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a file-backed ring buffer. The actual structure layout is intentionally hidden; it is managed via the provided API functions. Details of internal fields and lifetime semantics beyond init/deinit are not exposed in this header.

Ring buffer object managing a byte FIFO in a preallocated contiguous buffer. Fields track total capacity (size), current usage (used), bytes currently handed out but not yet consumed (in_flight), remaining available space (avail), and pointers to buffer bounds (begin, end) and moving positions (head for write position, tail for read position). Constructed and managed via the cs_rbuf_* API; internal fields should be treated as implementation details.

Broken-down time structure from the C standard library. It is only referenced here as a parameter type to cs_timegm; it is not defined in this header. Because the task requires only types explicitly defined in this header, there are no custom types to document.
8-bit unsigned integer type. Defined here as an alias of unsigned char only for older MSVC (<1700) on Windows; otherwise it is expected to come from <stdint.h>. Pointer form shown as required.
64-bit unsigned integer type. Defined here as an alias of unsigned __int64 only for older MSVC (<1700) on Windows; otherwise it is expected to come from <stdint.h>. Pointer form shown as required.

Forward-declared/externally defined output sink type used by Frozen’s json_printf. It is only referenced in this header via function prototype mg_json_printer_mbuf and the JSON_OUT_MBUF macro; no definition is provided here.
Externally defined growable memory buffer type from common/mbuf.h. Referenced by mg_json_emit_str and the JSON_OUT_MBUF macro; not defined in this header.
Externally defined immutable string/view type from common/mg_str.h. Used as an argument to mg_json_emit_str; not defined here.

Opaque directory stream handle used by this header when CS_DEFINE_DIRENT is defined. It is a typedef of an unnamed struct containing a dummy int, acting as a placeholder for platform-specific DIR implementations.
Directory entry structure returned by readdir. Contains an inode number (d_ino) and the entry name (d_name). The size of d_name depends on platform: MAX_PATH on Windows, 256 elsewhere in this header.
Note: No additional typedefs or classes are defined. The functions declared serve as constructors for DIR. This placeholder entry is not a separate type and can be ignored if not needed.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only contains preprocessor macros related to endian detection and C linkage guards.

objects.definition: typedef void (*cs_base64_putc_t)(char, void *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for outputting a single Base64-encoded character with an associated user data pointer. Implementations write the provided character to a sink (e.g., buffer, stream) using the user data for context.

Context for incremental Base64 encoding. Holds the output callback, a 3-byte staging chunk with its current size, and a user data pointer passed to the callback. Use with cs_base64_init, cs_base64_update, and cs_base64_finish to stream-encode data.
direct_api_constructors: void cs_base64_init(struct cs_base64_ctx *ctx, cs_base64_putc_t putc, void *user_data)

objects.description: Debug-tracing payload embedded in TAILQ heads/entries when QUEUE_MACRO_DEBUG is enabled. Records last and previous source locations (file/line) that modified the queue element or head. Present only when QUEUE_MACRO_DEBUG is defined; otherwise related macros are no-ops.

No custom struct, enum, typedef, or class types are defined in this header. The file defines a set of integer status macros (STATUS_OK, STATUS_..., etc.) and declares a function std::string StatusToString(int). Since macros are not types and no enums/structs/classes/typedefs are present, there are no custom data types to document. This placeholder entry is provided to explicitly note the absence of defined types.

A small utility class representing an operation status: an integer error code and an optional string message. ok() is true when code_ equals STATUS_OK (defined in included error_codes.h). Provides constructors, equality operators, and helper factories (OK, CANCELLED, UNIMPLEMENTED, UNKNOWN). ToString() serializes the status. Implementation details such as exact error code values come from common/util/error_codes.h and are not defined here.

objects.definition:
enum json_token_type {
  JSON_TYPE_INVALID = 0, /* memsetting to 0 should create INVALID value */
  JSON_TYPE_STRING,
  JSON_TYPE_NUMBER,
  JSON_TYPE_TRUE,
  JSON_TYPE_FALSE,
  JSON_TYPE_NULL,
  JSON_TYPE_OBJECT_START,
  JSON_TYPE_OBJECT_END,
  JSON_TYPE_ARRAY_START,
  JSON_TYPE_ARRAY_END,

  JSON_TYPES_CNT
};
objects.description: Enumeration of JSON token kinds produced and consumed by this API. Used to describe parts of a JSON document during scanning/walking (e.g., strings, numbers, booleans, structural delimiters).

Represents a slice of the original JSON input along with its type. ptr points into the source buffer and is not NUL-terminated; len is the span length; type is one of enum json_token_type. Used in callbacks and scanning results.
Function pointer type for SAX-style JSON walker callbacks. Called for each parsed token with contextual name/path and the token itself.
Abstracts a JSON output sink. Holds a printer callback and storage-specific union used by built-in printers for memory buffers or FILE* output. Used by json_printf-family and formatting helpers.

objects.definition: typedef int (*json_printf_callback_t)(struct json_out *, va_list *ap);
objects.description: Callback signature used with %M in json_printf/json_vprintf to emit custom-formatted JSON into a json_out sink, consuming additional arguments from a va_list.

objects.definition: typedef void (*json_scanner_t)(const char *str, int len, void *user_data);
objects.description: Callback signature for custom %M handlers in json_scanf/json_vscanf that parse a sub-span [str,len] with a user_data pointer.

Boolean type. On old MSVC compilers (<1700), bool is typedef’d to int with matching false/true enumerators; otherwise the standard <stdbool.h> is included. Note: this is a conditional typedef; on conforming compilers, bool is provided by <stdbool.h>.

functions.name: MG_MALLOC
functions.description: Macro indirection to the C allocator (defaults to malloc). Allocates size bytes of uninitialized storage and returns a pointer to the beginning of the block, or NULL on failure. Intended to allow overriding the allocator by defining MG_MALLOC before including this header.
requirements: size specifies the number of bytes to allocate; may be 0 (implementation-defined behavior).
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
Returned memory is uninitialized and must not be read before being written.
Memory returned by MG_MALLOC must be released with MG_FREE (or via MG_REALLOC with size 0 if the implementation frees on size 0).
Do not pass the returned pointer to a different deallocator than MG_FREE.
If a custom MG_MALLOC is provided by the application, its contract must be compatible with malloc.

functions.name: MG_CALLOC
functions.description: Macro indirection to the C zero-initializing allocator (defaults to calloc). Allocates an array for count elements of size bytes each, initializes all bits to zero, and returns a pointer to the block, or NULL on failure. Supports overriding by defining MG_CALLOC before including this header.
requirements: count and size specify the total byte size as count * size; the caller should ensure this multiplication does not overflow size_t.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
Returned memory is zero-initialized and must be freed with MG_FREE.
Do not pass the returned pointer to a different deallocator than MG_FREE.
If a custom MG_CALLOC is provided by the application, its contract should be compatible with calloc.

functions.name: MG_REALLOC
functions.description: Macro indirection to the C reallocator (defaults to realloc). Changes the size of the memory block pointed to by ptr to size bytes and returns a pointer to the (possibly moved) block, or NULL on failure. Allows overriding by defining MG_REALLOC before including this header.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a pointer previously allocated by MG_MALLOC, MG_CALLOC, or MG_REALLOC (or their overrides).
If size is 0, behavior follows realloc semantics (commonly frees ptr and returns NULL or a unique pointer); caller must not assume memory remains allocated.
On success, the returned pointer may differ from ptr and the old pointer becomes invalid; the caller must use only the returned pointer thereafter.
On failure (NULL return with size > 0), the original block referenced by ptr remains valid and unmodified; the caller must preserve ptr to avoid leaks.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
If a custom MG_REALLOC is provided by the application, its contract should be compatible with realloc.

functions.name: MG_FREE
functions.description: Macro indirection to the C deallocator (defaults to free). Releases the memory block pointed to by ptr, making it available for future allocations. Can be overridden by defining MG_FREE before including this header.
requirements: ptr may be NULL, in which case no action is taken.
If ptr is non-NULL, it must have been obtained from MG_MALLOC, MG_CALLOC, or MG_REALLOC (or their overrides) and not previously freed.
Do not free the same pointer more than once (no double-free).
After calling MG_FREE, the pointer value becomes invalid and must not be dereferenced or used in MG_REALLOC.
If a custom MG_FREE is provided by the application, its contract should be compatible with free.

functions.name: mg_mk_str
functions.description: Create an mg_str view from a NUL-terminated C string. If s is NULL, returns {NULL, 0}. No allocation is performed; the resulting mg_str points to the original memory.
requirements: If s is non-NULL, it must point to a valid NUL-terminated string.
If s is NULL, the result will have p == NULL and len == 0; callers must handle this case.
The returned mg_str references the original memory; ensure the underlying memory remains valid for the duration of use.

functions.name: mg_mk_str_n
functions.signature: struct mg_str mg_mk_str_n(const char *s, size_t len);
functions.description: Create an mg_str view from a pointer and an explicit length. No allocation is performed; the mg_str points to the provided memory and may reference non NUL-terminated data.
requirements: If s is NULL, len must be 0; otherwise s must be valid for at least len bytes.
The returned mg_str references the original memory; ensure the underlying memory remains valid and unmodified as needed for the duration of use.
len may be less than, equal to, or greater than the C-string length; the function does not validate content.

functions.name: mg_vcmp
functions.signature: int mg_vcmp(const struct mg_str *str2, const char *str1);
functions.description: Cross-platform strcmp-style comparison where the first string is provided as mg_str and the second as a NUL-terminated C string. Returns 0 if equal, <0 if str2 < str1, >0 if str2 > str1, following strcmp semantics.
requirements: str2 must be non-NULL; if str2->p is NULL then str2->len must be 0.
str1 must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid NUL-terminated string.
Comparison uses exactly str2->len bytes from str2 and characters in str1 up to NUL; callers should not assume either input is NUL-terminated beyond those bounds.

functions.name: mg_vcasecmp
functions.signature: int mg_vcasecmp(const struct mg_str *str2, const char *str1);
functions.description: Cross-platform, case-insensitive comparison analogous to strncasecmp, where the first string is provided as mg_str and the second as a NUL-terminated C string. Returns 0 if equal ignoring case, <0 or >0 otherwise.
requirements: str2 must be non-NULL; if str2->p is NULL then str2->len must be 0.
str1 must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid NUL-terminated string.
Comparison considers at most str2->len bytes from str2 and characters in str1 up to NUL, using case-insensitive rules.

functions.name: mg_strdup
functions.signature: struct mg_str mg_strdup(const struct mg_str s);
functions.description: Allocate and return a heap-allocated copy of s. The returned mg_str’s p points to newly allocated memory holding s.len bytes; len equals s.len.
requirements: If s.p is NULL, s.len must be 0; the function will allocate an empty string or return {NULL,0} depending on implementation (exact behavior unknown; treat as possibly allocating zero-length).
The caller is responsible for freeing the returned string via mg_strfree.
Do not pass the returned mg_str to free() directly unless library documentation guarantees compatibility; use mg_strfree.

functions.name: mg_strdup_nul
functions.signature: struct mg_str mg_strdup_nul(const struct mg_str s);
functions.description: Allocate and return a heap-allocated copy of s with an added NUL terminator. The NUL is not counted in len, but the memory at p[len] is NUL, making p safe to use as a C string.
requirements: If s.p is NULL, s.len must be 0; behavior for allocating empty string is library-defined (result will be NUL-terminated).
The caller must free the returned string with mg_strfree.
Do not assume any extra capacity beyond the single NUL terminator.

functions.name: mg_strchr
functions.signature: const char *mg_strchr(const struct mg_str s, int c);
functions.description: Locate the first occurrence of character c within the mg_str s. Searches at most s.len bytes and does not require NUL termination. Returns a pointer to the matching character within s.p, or NULL if not found.
requirements: If s.p is NULL, s.len must be 0; otherwise s.p must be valid for at least s.len bytes.
c is interpreted as an unsigned char value cast to int, consistent with standard strchr expectations.
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, aliases memory owned by the caller; ensure s’s storage remains valid while the pointer is used.

functions.name: mg_strcmp
functions.signature: int mg_strcmp(const struct mg_str str1, const struct mg_str str2);
functions.description: Compare two mg_str values using strcmp-like semantics. Returns 0 if equal, <0 if str1 < str2, >0 if str1 > str2.
requirements: If either str1.p or str2.p is NULL, the corresponding len must be 0; otherwise each pointer must be valid for at least its len bytes.
Comparison is based on byte values; NUL termination is not required and only len bytes of each are considered.

functions.name: mg_strncmp
functions.signature: int mg_strncmp(const struct mg_str str1, const struct mg_str str2, size_t n);
functions.description: Compare at most n bytes of two mg_str values, like strncmp. Returns 0 if the first min(n, len1, len2) bytes are equal (with usual semantics for length differences), <0 or >0 otherwise.
requirements: If either str1.p or str2.p is NULL, its len must be 0; otherwise each pointer must be valid for at least its len bytes.
Only up to n bytes are compared; callers should set n accordingly.

functions.name: mg_strcasecmp
functions.signature: int mg_strcasecmp(const struct mg_str str1, const struct mg_str str2);
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of two mg_str values; return value follows strcmp semantics while ignoring ASCII case.
requirements: If either str1.p or str2.p is NULL, its len must be 0; otherwise each pointer must be valid for at least its len bytes.
Case-insensitive rules are applied to the compared bytes; inputs need not be NUL-terminated.

functions.name: mg_strfree
functions.description: Free an mg_str previously allocated on the heap (e.g., by mg_strdup or mg_strdup_nul). After freeing, the function typically clears s to {NULL, 0} (exact postcondition not specified).
requirements: s must be non-NULL.
s->p must either be NULL or point to heap-allocated memory compatible with this library’s allocation strategy (e.g., returned by mg_strdup/mg_strdup_nul).
Do not call mg_strfree on mg_str values that merely reference external or static memory, stack data, or string literals.
After calling, the mg_str should not be used unless reinitialized.

functions.name: mg_strstr
functions.signature: const char *mg_strstr(const struct mg_str haystack, const struct mg_str needle);
functions.description: Find the first occurrence of the substring needle within haystack. Searches within haystack.p over haystack.len bytes. Returns a pointer to the start of the match within haystack.p, or NULL if not found.
requirements: If haystack.p is NULL, haystack.len must be 0; otherwise haystack.p must be valid for at least haystack.len bytes.
If needle.p is NULL, needle.len must be 0; otherwise needle.p must be valid for at least needle.len bytes.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, aliases haystack’s memory; ensure haystack storage remains valid while using it.

functions.name: mg_strstrip
functions.description: Return a view of s with leading and trailing whitespace removed. Typically adjusts p and len without allocating, so the returned mg_str references the original memory.
requirements: If s.p is NULL, s.len must be 0; otherwise s.p must be valid for at least s.len bytes.
The returned mg_str aliases the original storage; ensure the original buffer remains valid while the stripped view is used.
Whitespace definition and behavior on all locales are not specified; assume standard ASCII whitespace unless documented otherwise.

functions.name: mg_str_starts_with
functions.signature: int mg_str_starts_with(struct mg_str s, struct mg_str prefix);
functions.description: Return 1 if s starts with prefix, 0 otherwise. Comparison is byte-wise over prefix.len and does not require NUL termination.
requirements: If s.p is NULL, s.len must be 0; otherwise s.p must be valid for at least s.len bytes.
If prefix.p is NULL, prefix.len must be 0; otherwise prefix.p must be valid for at least prefix.len bytes.
Return value is 1 for true and 0 for false; no other values are documented.

functions.name: mbuf_init
functions.description: Initializes an mbuf structure with an initial capacity. Prepares the buffer for subsequent append/insert operations.
requirements: mb must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct mbuf (not NULL).
initial_capacity is a size_t; no explicit minimum is stated.
Call before using mb with other mbuf APIs that assume initialization.

functions.name: mbuf_free
functions.description: Frees any memory allocated for the mbuf and resets the mbuf structure to an empty state.
requirements: mb must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct mbuf (not NULL).
Safe usage after mbuf_init or after previous mbuf operations; behavior on never-initialized mb is not documented.
Do not use mb->buf after this call; the buffer is freed and mb is reset.

functions.name: mbuf_append
functions.signature: size_t mbuf_append(struct mbuf *mb, const void *data, size_t data_size);
functions.description: Appends data to the end of the mbuf, growing the buffer as needed. Returns the number of bytes appended, or 0 on out-of-memory.
requirements: mb must be initialized via mbuf_init (or otherwise in a valid state).
If data_size > 0, data must point to at least data_size readable bytes; if data_size == 0, data may be NULL.
Caller should check the return value: 0 indicates append failed due to OOM.

functions.name: mbuf_append_and_free
functions.signature: size_t mbuf_append_and_free(struct mbuf *mb, void *data, size_t data_size);
functions.description: Appends heap-allocated data to the mbuf and frees the source buffer regardless of success. Returns the number of bytes appended, or 0 on out-of-memory.
requirements: mb must be initialized via mbuf_init (or otherwise in a valid state).
data must be heap-allocated and valid for reading data_size bytes; it will be freed irrespective of return value.
If data_size == 0, data may be NULL; it will still be considered for freeing per documentation note.
Caller should check the return value: 0 indicates append failed due to OOM.

functions.name: mbuf_insert
functions.signature: size_t mbuf_insert(struct mbuf *mb, size_t off, const void *data, size_t data_size);
functions.description: Inserts data at the specified offset within the mbuf, shifting existing data forward and growing the buffer if necessary. Returns the number of bytes inserted.
requirements: mb must be initialized and in a valid state.
If data_size > 0, data must point to at least data_size readable bytes; if data_size == 0, data may be NULL.
Offset off should be within the current data range (inferred): 0 <= off <= mb->len; behavior for out-of-range offsets is not documented.
Caller should expect existing data at and after off to be shifted forward by data_size bytes.

functions.name: mbuf_remove
functions.description: Removes data_size bytes from the beginning of the buffer, effectively advancing the start of valid data.
requirements: mb must be initialized and in a valid state.
data_size should not exceed mb->len (inferred); behavior if data_size > mb->len is not documented.
After removal, previously removed bytes become invalid and must not be accessed.

functions.name: mbuf_resize
functions.description: Resizes the mbuf's underlying buffer to new_size. If new_size is smaller than the current data length (len), the resize is not performed.
requirements: mb must be initialized and in a valid state.
If caller needs resize to succeed, new_size must be >= mb->len (explicitly documented).
Caller should not assume a shrink occurs when new_size < mb->len; buffer remains unchanged in that case.

functions.name: mbuf_move
functions.description: Moves the internal state (buffer pointer, length, capacity) from one mbuf to another, leaving the source in a reset/empty state. Useful for transferring ownership without copying.
requirements: from and to must be valid pointers to struct mbuf.
Behavior regarding pre-existing contents of 'to' is not documented; callers should ensure 'to' is empty or no longer needed before calling (inferred).
After the call, do not use the old contents of 'from'; it is considered moved and reset.

functions.name: mbuf_clear
functions.description: Removes all data from the mbuf, making its length zero. Capacity may be retained.
requirements: mb must be initialized and in a valid state.
After clearing, mb->len becomes 0; caller should not assume capacity is reduced.

functions.name: mbuf_trim
functions.description: Shrinks the mbuf's allocated size to match its current length (size := len), releasing any extra capacity.
requirements: mb must be initialized and in a valid state.
Only reduces capacity; does not change mb->len or data contents.

functions.name: c_strnlen
functions.description: Equivalent of the standard strnlen: returns the length of the string s, limited to at most maxlen characters. Intended for safe length checks when the string may be unterminated within maxlen.
requirements: s must be a valid, readable pointer; behavior is undefined if s is NULL.
maxlen is the maximum number of characters to examine; function returns a value in [0, maxlen].

functions.name: c_snprintf
functions.signature: int c_snprintf(char *buf, size_t buf_size, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Equivalent of the standard snprintf: formats a string according to format and writes it into buf, writing at most buf_size bytes including the terminating NUL. Returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding the terminating NUL), which may be greater than buf_size-1 if truncation occurred.
requirements: If buf_size > 0, buf must point to a writable memory buffer of at least buf_size bytes.
format must be a valid NUL-terminated format string.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in format.
buf may be NULL only if buf_size is 0.

functions.name: c_vsnprintf
functions.signature: int c_vsnprintf(char *buf, size_t buf_size, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Equivalent of the standard vsnprintf: same as c_snprintf but takes a va_list ap instead of variadic arguments. Returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding the NUL).
requirements: If buf_size > 0, buf must point to a writable memory buffer of at least buf_size bytes.
format must be a valid NUL-terminated format string.
ap must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to format.
buf may be NULL only if buf_size is 0.

functions.name: c_strnstr
functions.signature: const char *c_strnstr(const char *s, const char *find, size_t slen);
functions.description: Searches for the first occurrence of the substring find within the first slen characters of the string s. Returns a pointer to the start of the match within s, or NULL if not found.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated or sufficiently long readable buffer; behavior is undefined if s is NULL.
find must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer; behavior is undefined if find is NULL.
Search is limited to at most slen characters from s.

functions.name: cs_to_hex
functions.signature: void cs_to_hex(char *to, const unsigned char *p, size_t len);
functions.description: Converts binary data (p, len) to a lowercase hexadecimal string representation in to. Each input byte becomes two hex characters and the output is NUL-terminated. Intended for stringifying binary blobs.
requirements: to must point to a writable buffer of size at least 2*len + 1 bytes.
p must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
Output will be NUL-terminated at to[2*len].

functions.name: cs_from_hex
functions.signature: void cs_from_hex(char *to, const char *p, size_t len);
functions.description: Converts a hex-encoded string p back to binary into to. This is the reverse of cs_to_hex. Produces len/2 bytes of binary output from len hex characters; output is not NUL-terminated.
requirements: p must point to a readable buffer containing exactly len hexadecimal characters (0-9, a-f, A-F).
len must be even; each pair of hex characters is converted to one output byte.
to must point to a writable buffer large enough for at least len/2 bytes.
Behavior is undefined for non-hex input characters.

functions.name: strdup
functions.description: Equivalent of the standard strdup, defined only when CS_ENABLE_STRDUP is 1: allocates a new NUL-terminated string that is a copy of src. Caller owns the returned buffer and must free it.
requirements: This declaration is present and usable only if the macro CS_ENABLE_STRDUP is enabled at compile time.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer; behavior is undefined if src is NULL.
The returned pointer must be freed by the caller (with free).
On allocation failure, returns NULL; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: cs_to64
functions.description: Simple string-to-int64 conversion routine, defined only when CS_ENABLE_TO64 is 1. Parses s and returns its int64 value. Exact parsing rules are not documented; typically supports optional sign and decimal digits.
requirements: This declaration is present and usable only if the macro CS_ENABLE_TO64 is enabled at compile time.
s must be a valid NUL-terminated string pointer; behavior is undefined if s is NULL.
Callers must handle potential out-of-range or malformed input according to the implementation’s return behavior (details not documented).

functions.name: mg_ncasecmp
functions.signature: int mg_ncasecmp(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t len);
functions.description: Cross-platform version of strncasecmp: case-insensitive comparison of at most len characters of s1 and s2. Returns <0, 0, or >0 if s1 is lexicographically less than, equal to, or greater than s2 (case-insensitive).
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid pointers to readable buffers; behavior is undefined if either is NULL.
len limits the maximum number of characters compared.

functions.name: mg_casecmp
functions.description: Cross-platform version of strcasecmp: case-insensitive comparison of NUL-terminated strings s1 and s2. Returns <0, 0, or >0 if s1 is lexicographically less than, equal to, or greater than s2 (case-insensitive).
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid NUL-terminated strings; behavior is undefined if either is NULL.

functions.name: mg_asprintf
functions.signature: int mg_asprintf(char **buf, size_t size, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Formats a string into the buffer pointed to by *buf. If the provided buffer (size bytes) is large enough, writes into it and leaves *buf unchanged. If it is too small, allocates a sufficiently large heap buffer, writes into it, updates *buf to point to the new buffer, and returns the number of characters written (excluding the NUL). This avoids heap allocation for small outputs.
requirements: buf must be non-NULL and point to a valid char* variable.
*buf must either be NULL or point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes; if size is 0, *buf may be NULL and the function will allocate.
fmt must be a valid NUL-terminated format string; variadic arguments must match fmt.
If the function allocates a new buffer, the caller becomes the owner and must free(*buf) when done.
The returned value is the number of characters written (excluding the NUL) or a negative value on error; callers should handle negative returns.

functions.name: mg_avprintf
functions.signature: int mg_avprintf(char **buf, size_t size, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Same as mg_asprintf but takes a va_list. Writes into *buf if the provided buffer is large enough; otherwise allocates a new heap buffer and updates *buf. Returns the number of characters written (excluding the NUL), or a negative value on error.
requirements: buf must be non-NULL and point to a valid char* variable.
*buf must either be NULL or point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes; if size is 0, *buf may be NULL and the function will allocate.
fmt must be a valid NUL-terminated format string.
ap must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to fmt.
If a new buffer is allocated, the caller must free(*buf) when done.
Callers should handle negative return values as errors.

functions.name: mg_next_comma_list_entry
functions.signature: const char *mg_next_comma_list_entry(const char *list, struct mg_str *val, struct mg_str *eq_val);
functions.description: Traverses a comma-separated list of entries in list without copying. On each call, extracts the next entry into val; if the entry has the form "x=y", eq_val is set to the "y" part and val is adjusted to "x". Returns a pointer to the position in list after the parsed entry (to pass to the next call), or NULL at end. Intended for parsing strings like "aa,bb,cc" efficiently.
requirements: list must point to a readable NUL-terminated string; pass the returned pointer from the previous call to continue. Passing NULL indicates end.
val and eq_val must be non-NULL pointers to struct mg_str to receive the results.
The underlying memory for list must remain valid for as long as val->p and eq_val->p are used; returned mg_strs point into the original list.
If the list is simple entries like "aa,bb,cc", eq_val will have length 0.

functions.name: mg_next_comma_list_entry_n
functions.signature: struct mg_str mg_next_comma_list_entry_n(struct mg_str list, struct mg_str *val, struct mg_str *eq_val);
functions.description: Like mg_next_comma_list_entry but takes list as struct mg_str. Parses the next comma-separated entry, setting val to the key and eq_val to the value if the entry is of the form "x=y" (otherwise eq_val length is 0). Returns the remaining list segment to continue iteration. Note: test the returned .p, not .len; on the last iteration that yields a result, .len will be 0 but .p will not; when finished, .p will be NULL.
requirements: val and eq_val must be non-NULL pointers to struct mg_str to receive results.
list.p must point to a readable buffer that remains valid while val->p and eq_val->p are used.
Callers must follow the documented iteration contract: continue while returned .p is not NULL; do not rely solely on .len.

functions.name: mg_next_query_string_entry_n
functions.signature: struct mg_str mg_next_query_string_entry_n(struct mg_str list, struct mg_str *val, struct mg_str *eq_val);
functions.description: Helper for parsing query strings represented as struct mg_str. Splits entries on '&' and splits keys and values on '='. Does not perform URL decoding/unescaping. Returns the remaining list segment to continue iteration; results are provided via val and eq_val.
requirements: val and eq_val must be non-NULL pointers to struct mg_str.
list.p must point to a readable buffer that remains valid while val->p and eq_val->p are used.
No unescaping is performed; callers must decode percent-encoded data separately if needed.
Iterate while the returned .p is not NULL.

functions.name: mg_match_prefix
functions.signature: size_t mg_match_prefix(const char *pattern, int pattern_len, const char *str);
functions.description: Matches the NUL-terminated glob pattern against the prefix of str in a case-insensitive manner, using these glob rules: '*' matches zero or more characters up to '/', '**' matches zero or more characters including '/', '?' matches exactly one non-'/' character, and '|' or ',' separate alternatives. Returns the number of bytes matched (0 on no match). The second argument is the length of str to consider (despite the parameter name).
requirements: pattern must be a valid NUL-terminated pattern string; behavior is undefined if NULL.
str must be a valid NUL-terminated string; behavior is undefined if NULL.
pattern_len must be the maximum number of characters from str to consider and must be >= 0.
Match is case-insensitive and respects the described glob syntax.

functions.name: mg_match_prefix_n
functions.signature: size_t mg_match_prefix_n(const struct mg_str pattern, const struct mg_str str);
functions.description: Like mg_match_prefix but takes pattern and str as struct mg_str. Applies the same glob rules in a case-insensitive manner and returns the number of bytes matched (0 on no match).
requirements: pattern.p and str.p must point to readable buffers described by their respective lengths.
Glob rules are the same as documented for mg_match_prefix; matching is case-insensitive.

functions.name: cs_log_set_level
functions.description: Sets the global maximum log level; messages with a higher level are suppressed. Typical usage is at program startup to control verbosity.
requirements: level must be a valid value of enum cs_log_level (e.g., LL_ERROR..LL_VERBOSE_DEBUG).
Takes effect process-wide/global for this logging subsystem.

functions.name: cs_log_set_file_level
functions.description: Configures per-file log levels using a comma-separated list of prefix=level rules. A prefix is matched against the printed log prefix (including filename and line); first match wins, otherwise the default level applies. Example: "mongoose.c=1,mjs.c=1,=4".
requirements: file_level must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string containing comma-separated entries of the form prefix=level.
prefix may be empty to specify a default rule (e.g., "=4").
level values should be integers consistent with enum cs_log_level values.

functions.name: cs_log_print_prefix
functions.signature: int cs_log_print_prefix(enum cs_log_level level, const char *fname, int line);
functions.description: Helper that decides whether a message at the given level should be printed based on the current global level and filters; if so, prints the log prefix (including file and line) and returns 1, otherwise returns 0. Intended to be used by the LOG macro before formatting the message.
requirements: level must be a valid enum cs_log_level.
fname must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated C string (typically __FILE__).
line should be a non-negative source line number (typically __LINE__).
Callers should print the message only if the return value is non-zero.

functions.name: cs_log_set_file
functions.description: Sets the FILE stream to which logs are written. If file is NULL, logs are written to stderr.
requirements: Available only when CS_ENABLE_STDIO is enabled at build time.
If file is non-NULL, it must be a valid, open FILE* suitable for writing and remain valid while in use by the logger.
If file is NULL, logging redirects to stderr.

functions.name: cs_log_printf
functions.description: Formats and writes a log message to the current log file/stream, appends a newline, and flushes the stream. Intended to be called after cs_log_print_prefix indicates the message should be logged.
requirements: Available only when CS_ENABLE_STDIO is enabled at build time.
fmt must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated format string compatible with printf-style formatting.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.
The function appends a trailing newline and flushes the stream; callers should not include a final newline unless desired redundantly.

functions.name: cs_read_file
functions.description: Reads the entire contents of the file at path into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated memory buffer. The file size (excluding the terminating NUL) is written to *size. Returns the allocated buffer on success or NULL on error. Typical usage: call, check for NULL, use the data (size bytes; note the trailing '\0' is not counted in size), then free() the buffer.
requirements: path must be a valid C string pointing to a readable file path.
size must be a non-NULL pointer to size_t; on success the file size (not counting the terminating '\0') is written to *size.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect errors.
On success, caller must free() the returned buffer when no longer needed.
The returned buffer is NUL-terminated; do not assume size includes the terminator.

functions.name: cs_mmap_file
functions.description: On platforms that support memory-mapped files and when compiled with CS_MMAP, maps the file at path into memory and returns the mapped address. The file size is written to *size. Availability is conditional on CS_MMAP. The header does not document the error return convention or unmapping requirements; callers should treat a NULL result as an error and manage the mapping according to the library/platform’s conventions.
requirements: This function is available only when CS_MMAP is defined and the platform supports memory-mapped files.
path must be a valid C string pointing to an existing file that can be mapped.
size must be a non-NULL pointer to size_t; the file size is written to *size.
Caller should defensively check the return value (e.g., for NULL) to detect errors, as error semantics are not explicitly documented.

functions.name: cs_hex_decode
functions.signature: int cs_hex_decode(const char *s, int len, unsigned char *dst, int *dst_len);
functions.description: Decode a hex-encoded byte sequence from s of length len into the buffer dst. The decoded length is written to *dst_len. The return value is the number of processed bytes from the input; a return value equal to len indicates all input was successfully processed. Typical usage: allocate a sufficiently large dst (at least len/2 bytes for well-formed hex), pass the source pointer and length, and read the decoded size from dst_len.
requirements: s must point to at least len bytes of accessible memory containing a hex-encoded string.
len must be the exact number of bytes to read from s.
dst must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the decoded output (for well-formed hex, capacity should be at least len/2 bytes).
dst_len must be a valid, non-null pointer to an int and writable; on return, *dst_len receives the number of decoded bytes written to dst.
Callers must check the return value: if it equals len, all input was processed; otherwise, not all input was consumed.
Behavior for invalid (non-hex) characters or odd-length input is not documented here; callers should ensure s contains valid hex data.

functions.name: cs_crc32
functions.signature: uint32_t cs_crc32(uint32_t crc, const void *data, uint32_t len);
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit CRC over a buffer, starting from the supplied initial CRC value. Typical usage is to pass 0 for the first chunk, and the previously returned CRC for subsequent chunks to compute a rolling CRC over multiple buffers. The function reads, but does not modify, the memory referenced by data and returns the resulting CRC32 value.
requirements: data must point to a buffer that is at least len bytes long.
If len > 0, data must be non-null.
len is the number of bytes to process and must fit in a uint32_t.
The crc parameter is the initial CRC state; pass 0 to start a fresh CRC computation or the prior return value to continue over additional data.

functions.name: cs_frbuf_init
functions.description: Create and initialize a file-backed ring buffer stored at the file path fname with a capacity related to size. Returns an opaque handle to the ring buffer on success, or NULL on failure. Typical usage: call this once to obtain a buffer handle, then use cs_frbuf_append and cs_frbuf_get, and finally cs_frbuf_deinit to clean up. Detailed on-disk layout, persistence, and exact capacity semantics are not documented in this header.
requirements: fname must point to a valid, null-terminated path string to the file to be used for backing storage.
size must be a non-zero 16-bit unsigned value (0–65535); practical minimum/maximum capacity semantics are unknown.
The returned struct cs_frbuf* must be checked for NULL to detect initialization failure.
The returned handle must be passed to other cs_frbuf_* functions and eventually to cs_frbuf_deinit.
Must be called before any other operation on the ring buffer handle.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown from this header.

functions.name: cs_frbuf_deinit
functions.description: Tear down and release resources associated with a file-backed ring buffer previously created by cs_frbuf_init. Intended to close any underlying file descriptors and free memory. No value is returned.
requirements: b must be a handle previously returned by cs_frbuf_init (not an arbitrary pointer).
Do not use the handle b after calling cs_frbuf_deinit.
It is unknown whether passing NULL is allowed; callers should avoid passing NULL unless implementation guarantees it is safe.
Thread-safety during concurrent use with other operations is unknown.

functions.name: cs_frbuf_append
functions.signature: bool cs_frbuf_append(struct cs_frbuf *b, const void *data, uint16_t len);
functions.description: Append len bytes from data to the end of the file-backed ring buffer identified by b. Returns true on success, false on failure (e.g., I/O error or invalid arguments). Whether the buffer overwrites old data on overflow, blocks, or fails is not specified in this header.
requirements: b must be a valid handle obtained from cs_frbuf_init and not yet deinitialized.
data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory; data must not be NULL if len > 0.
len is a 16-bit unsigned length (0–65535). Semantics for len == 0 are unspecified.
Behavior when len exceeds the buffer's capacity is not documented; callers should not assume implicit truncation or overwrite.
Return value must be checked; false indicates the append did not take effect.

functions.name: cs_frbuf_get
functions.description: Retrieve the next record or chunk from the file-backed ring buffer b. On success, returns a non-negative integer (likely the number of bytes) and sets *data to point to that data; on empty buffer or error, returns a negative value or possibly 0 depending on implementation. The ownership and lifetime of the memory referenced by *data, and whether the caller must free it, are not documented in this header.
requirements: b must be a valid handle obtained from cs_frbuf_init and not yet deinitialized.
data must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* variable where the function can store the resulting data pointer.
The meaning of the return value (length vs. status) and error codes is not specified; callers must consult implementation to determine empty/error conditions and memory ownership.

It is unknown whether the returned pointer is valid only until the next operation, must be freed by the caller, or refers to internal storage; callers should treat ownership semantics as unknown without further documentation.

functions.name: cs_rbuf_init
functions.description: Initialize a ring buffer object with the given capacity in bytes. Likely allocates or sets up internal storage and resets head/tail and counters. Intended to be called before any other cs_rbuf_* operation and paired with cs_rbuf_deinit when done. Details like allocation strategy and error reporting are not documented here.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to a cs_rbuf_t storage location.
size is expected to be the desired capacity in bytes; non-zero is recommended (exact constraints are not documented).
Must be called before any other operation on b.
If this allocates internal memory, callers should later call cs_rbuf_deinit(b) to release resources (inferred).
Thread-safety and reentrancy guarantees are unknown.

functions.name: cs_rbuf_deinit
functions.description: Tear down a ring buffer previously initialized with cs_rbuf_init, releasing any resources and invalidating pointers. After this call, the buffer should not be used unless re-initialized. Specifics about double-free safety or idempotency are not documented here.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer that has been successfully initialized by cs_rbuf_init (inferred).
After calling, do not use b (except to reinitialize).
Safe use in the presence of in-flight data or concurrent access is unknown.

functions.name: cs_rbuf_clear
functions.description: Clear the ring buffer’s contents, making it empty without destroying the buffer. Typically resets used/in-flight counters and head/tail positions while preserving capacity. Behavior with respect to data loss is as expected: existing buffered data becomes unavailable.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized cs_rbuf_t (inferred).
Any outstanding pointers previously obtained from cs_rbuf_get or cs_rbuf_contig_tail_space may become invalid after clearing (inferred).
Thread-safety is unknown; avoid concurrent readers/writers unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: cs_rbuf_append
functions.signature: void cs_rbuf_append(cs_rbuf_t *b, const void *data, uint16_t len);
functions.description: Append len bytes to the ring buffer from the memory region data. Intended for pushing arbitrary payloads into the buffer. The amount accepted when len exceeds available capacity, and whether data is dropped, truncated, or overwrites old data, is not specified in this header.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized cs_rbuf_t (inferred).
If len > 0, data should be a valid, non-null pointer to at least len bytes readable memory.
The caller should ensure there is sufficient free space before appending; behavior when len exceeds available capacity is unspecified here (inferred).
Not thread-safe unless documented elsewhere; avoid concurrent modifications.

functions.name: cs_rbuf_append_one
functions.description: Append a single byte to the ring buffer. Convenience wrapper around cs_rbuf_append for one byte. Behavior when the buffer is full is not specified in this header.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized cs_rbuf_t (inferred).
Caller should ensure there is at least one byte of free space; behavior on overflow is unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: cs_rbuf_at
functions.description: Return the byte at logical index i within the buffer’s stored data. Likely indexes from the current head (oldest) toward tail. Bounds checking behavior is unspecified here; whether the function asserts, wraps, or returns undefined data for out-of-range i is unknown.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized cs_rbuf_t (inferred).
i is expected to be within the current used range [0, used-1]; behavior otherwise is unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: cs_rbuf_get
functions.description: Obtain a pointer to up to max contiguous bytes currently available to read from the buffer, returning the actual contiguous byte count. Typically used to access readable data without copying; the caller should subsequently call cs_rbuf_consume to advance the head by the number of bytes processed. Exact semantics when no data is available are not documented but commonly return 0 and set *data to a valid pointer or leave it unchanged.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized cs_rbuf_t (inferred).
data should be a non-null pointer to a uint8_t* location to receive the address of the readable span (inferred).
max specifies an upper bound on the number of bytes to expose; expected to be >= 1 for meaningful results (inferred).
The returned pointer (via *data) remains valid only until the buffer is modified (e.g., by consume, append, clear); do not retain it beyond that (inferred).
Caller should call cs_rbuf_consume with the number of bytes actually processed to advance the head (inferred).

functions.name: cs_rbuf_consume
functions.description: Advance the buffer’s head by len bytes, marking data as consumed. Typically paired with cs_rbuf_get to discard bytes after processing. Behavior if len exceeds the number of bytes currently available is not specified here.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized cs_rbuf_t (inferred).
len should not exceed the current number of readable bytes; behavior otherwise is unspecified (inferred).
Do not consume more bytes than were obtained from the previous cs_rbuf_get call when using the contiguous read pattern (inferred).

functions.name: cs_rbuf_contig_tail_space
functions.description: Return the number of contiguous free bytes available at the tail (write end) without wrapping, and provide a pointer to the start of that writable region via data. Typically used for zero-copy writes: the caller writes up to the returned amount then calls cs_rbuf_advance_tail to commit the bytes. Behavior when the buffer is full likely returns 0; specifics are not documented here.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized cs_rbuf_t (inferred).
data should be a non-null pointer to a uint8_t* location to receive the writable pointer (inferred).
Caller must not write more than the returned number of bytes into the provided region before calling cs_rbuf_advance_tail (inferred).
Any pointer obtained remains valid only until the buffer is modified or wrapped (inferred).

functions.name: cs_rbuf_advance_tail
functions.description: Commit len newly written bytes at the tail, advancing the write pointer and increasing the used count. This usually follows cs_rbuf_contig_tail_space after the caller has written data into the provided region.
requirements: b must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized cs_rbuf_t (inferred).
len should be less than or equal to the amount previously indicated by cs_rbuf_contig_tail_space and actually written by the caller; behavior otherwise is unspecified (inferred).
Must not advance beyond the buffer’s capacity; overflow behavior is unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: cs_time
functions.description: Returns the current wall-clock time as seconds since the Unix Epoch with sub-second granularity. Intended as a convenience alternative to time() that provides fractional seconds. Monotonicity, time zone handling, and error signaling are not documented; treat the value as wall-clock (system) time in seconds as a double.
requirements: No input arguments or preconditions are required.
Callers should not assume the value is monotonic or immune to system clock changes (not documented).
Precision, range, and error conditions are unspecified; callers should be prepared for typical double precision limits and platform-dependent behavior (unknown).

functions.name: cs_timegm
functions.description: Converts a broken-down time (struct tm) to seconds since the Unix Epoch, similar to the non-standard timegm (interpreting the input as UTC). Returns the result as a double. Exact overflow behavior, error signaling, and normalization rules are not documented.
requirements: tm must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid struct tm.
tm should represent a valid calendar time; field normalization and range handling are unspecified (unknown).
Interpretation is UTC (inferred from timegm semantics); callers should not expect local time or time zone adjustments.

functions.name: cs_varint_llen
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to encode the given 64-bit unsigned integer using this library’s varint format. Typical usage: call to determine the encoded length prior to allocating a buffer or to size-check an existing buffer.
requirements: Argument num may be any 64-bit unsigned integer.
No side effects; does not write to memory.
Returned size indicates the full length required to encode num in this varint format.

functions.name: cs_varint_encode
functions.signature: size_t cs_varint_encode(uint64_t num, uint8_t *buf, size_t buf_size);
functions.description: Encodes the given 64-bit unsigned integer into the provided buffer using this library’s varint format. Returns the total number of bytes that would be required to encode the value; this may be greater than buf_size, and in that case only buf_size bytes are written. Typical usage: first call cs_varint_llen or call once with a possibly small buffer, then allocate or validate buffer size and call again if needed.
requirements: If buf_size > 0, buf must be a valid, writable pointer to at least buf_size bytes.
If buf_size == 0, no bytes are written; the return value still reflects the full encoded length.
Caller should compare the return value with buf_size; if return value > buf_size, not all encoded bytes were written and the caller must provide a larger buffer to get the full encoding.
Argument num may be any 64-bit unsigned integer.
The varint format is library-specific; consumers must decode with matching cs_varint_decode/cs_varint_decode_unsafe.

functions.name: cs_varint_decode
functions.signature: bool cs_varint_decode(const uint8_t *buf, size_t buf_size, uint64_t *num, size_t *llen);
functions.description: Decodes a varint from the given buffer into num and stores the number of bytes consumed in llen. Returns true on successful decode; returns false if there are not enough bytes in buf to decode a complete value. Typical usage: pass a pointer to the start of an encoded varint and its available length, then check the return value before using outputs.
requirements: buf must point to at least buf_size readable bytes.
num must be a non-null pointer to receive the decoded value on success.
llen must be a non-null pointer to receive the number of bytes consumed on success (and per documentation is used to report length).
Caller must check the boolean return value; if false, the buffer did not contain a complete varint and outputs should not be used.
The buffer contents must be in this library’s varint format; decoding other formats is unsupported.

functions.name: cs_varint_decode_unsafe
functions.description: Decodes a varint from buf without explicit bounds checking and returns the decoded value; writes the number of bytes consumed to llen. Intended for scenarios where the caller guarantees that buf contains a complete, well-formed varint. Unsafe because it may read past the provided memory if the input is incomplete or malformed.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer containing a complete, well-formed varint in this library’s format; insufficient or malformed data results in undefined behavior.
buf must be a valid readable pointer; the function may read multiple bytes until the varint terminator is found.
llen must be a non-null pointer to an int where the function stores the number of bytes consumed.
Caller must ensure bounds safety externally; no buf_size is provided or checked.

functions.name: mg_json_printer_mbuf
functions.signature: int mg_json_printer_mbuf(struct json_out *out, const char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Printer callback compatible with Frozen’s json_printf that appends the provided buffer to an mbuf. Intended to be used via the JSON_OUT_MBUF(...) helper to direct json_printf output into a struct mbuf. Typical usage: construct a struct json_out with JSON_OUT_MBUF(&your_mbuf) and pass it to json_printf; this function will be invoked to append chunks to the mbuf.
requirements: out must point to a valid struct json_out configured to target an mbuf (e.g., created with JSON_OUT_MBUF(&mbuf)).
buf must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
The target struct mbuf must be properly initialized before use so it can grow/append data.
Caller should expect the return value to represent the number of bytes consumed/written; precise error signaling is unknown from this header.

functions.name: mg_json_emit_str
functions.signature: void mg_json_emit_str(struct mbuf *b, const struct mg_str s, int quote);
functions.description: Appends a string to the given mbuf, optionally JSON-quoting it. When quote is non-zero, the function emits the string surrounded by double quotes and (by convention) suitable for JSON; when zero, it appends the raw string. Intended for building JSON payloads directly into an mbuf.
requirements: b must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized struct mbuf that can accept appended data.
s.ptr must reference at least s.len bytes of readable memory (unknown whether NULL is allowed when s.len == 0).
quote controls quoting behavior; expected values are 0 (unquoted) or non-zero (quoted).
Caller is responsible for ensuring the mbuf has enough capacity or that it can be grown; error behavior is not specified in this header.

functions.name: opendir
functions.description: Opens a directory stream for iterating directory entries, analogous to POSIX opendir. Use it to obtain a DIR handle that can be passed to readdir to enumerate entries and to closedir to release the stream. Details of error reporting and ownership are not documented here; based on standard naming patterns, NULL is typically returned on failure.
requirements: dir_name must be a valid, null-terminated path string to an existing directory.
The returned DIR* (if non-NULL) must be closed with closedir when no longer needed.
Do not pass a NULL pointer for dir_name.
This API is available only when CS_DEFINE_DIRENT is defined at compile time (per header guard).
On Windows, directory entry names produced by readdir are limited to MAX_PATH characters; on non-Windows, to 256 characters (per struct dirent in this header).

functions.name: closedir
functions.description: Closes a directory stream previously opened with opendir, analogous to POSIX closedir. After closing, the DIR handle must not be used. Return value semantics are not documented here; by convention, 0 indicates success and a nonzero value indicates failure, but exact behavior is unknown.
requirements: dir must be a DIR* previously returned by a successful call to opendir.
dir must not be NULL.
After closedir returns, dir must not be used with readdir or closed again.
This API is available only when CS_DEFINE_DIRENT is defined at compile time (per header guard).

functions.name: readdir
functions.description: Reads the next directory entry from an open directory stream, analogous to POSIX readdir, returning a pointer to a struct dirent describing the entry. When the end of the directory is reached or on error, NULL is typically returned, though exact error reporting is not documented here. The struct dirent here contains d_ino and a fixed-size d_name buffer (MAX_PATH on Windows, 256 otherwise). Lifetime/ownership of the returned pointer is not specified in this header and is assumed to follow typical readdir patterns (valid until the next call on the same DIR or until closed), but exact details are unknown.
requirements: dir must be a DIR* previously returned by a successful call to opendir.
dir must not be NULL.
Callers should expect that entry names are truncated to the fixed-size d_name buffer defined here (MAX_PATH on Windows, 256 on non-Windows).
The returned pointer may be NULL to indicate end-of-directory or an error (exact differentiation is unknown).

functions.name: cs_base64_init
functions.signature: void cs_base64_init(struct cs_base64_ctx *ctx, cs_base64_putc_t putc, void *user_data);
functions.description: Initializes a streaming Base64 encoder context with a caller-provided output callback and user_data. Call this before feeding input via cs_base64_update and finalize with cs_base64_finish. The callback is invoked for each output character generated during encoding.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct cs_base64_ctx.

functions.name: cs_base64_update

requirements: ctx must have been initialized by a successful cs_base64_init call.

Do not call after cs_base64_finish has been called on the same ctx.

functions.name: cs_base64_finish

requirements: ctx must have been initialized by cs_base64_init.
Must be called after the final cs_base64_update to flush remaining data.
Do not reuse ctx for another encoding session without reinitializing with cs_base64_init.

functions.name: cs_base64_encode
functions.signature: void cs_base64_encode(const unsigned char *src, int src_len, char *dst, int *enc_len);
functions.description: One-shot Base64-encodes the src buffer of length src_len into dst and writes the resulting encoded length to *enc_len. Intended for callers that have the complete input and a destination buffer ready, as an alternative to the streaming API.
requirements: src must point to at least src_len bytes of readable data; src_len must be >= 0 (inferred from int length).

dst must have enough space to hold the Base64 output; typical requirement is at least 4 * ((src_len + 2) / 3) bytes, plus 1 if a terminating NUL is written (exact NUL-termination behavior is not documented here).
enc_len must be a valid, writable pointer to int to receive the encoded length.
Behavior regarding NUL-termination of dst is not specified in this header; callers should not assume a trailing NUL unless verified in implementation.

functions.name: cs_fprint_base64
functions.signature: void cs_fprint_base64(FILE *f, const unsigned char *src, int src_len);

requirements: f must be a valid, open FILE* suitable for writing.
src must point to at least src_len bytes of readable data; src_len must be >= 0 (inferred from int length).

functions.name: cs_base64_decode
functions.signature: int cs_base64_decode(const unsigned char *s, int len, char *dst, int *dec_len);
functions.description: Decodes a Base64 string s of length len into dst. dst must have enough space to hold the decoded result. On return, *dec_len is set to the number of bytes written to dst, and the function returns the number of processed bytes from s. A return value equal to len indicates that all input was successfully processed.
requirements: s must point to at least len bytes of readable data; len must be >= 0 (inferred from int length).

dec_len must be a valid, writable pointer to int to receive the decoded length.
Caller should check the return value: if it is less than len, only that many bytes from s were processed; if equal to len, the whole input was processed successfully as documented.
