functions.description: Copy-assignment operator. Replaces this Status with the contents of another and returns a reference to this object.
requirements: other must be a valid, initialized Status object.
Self-assignment is permitted.

functions.name: mgos::Status::OK
functions.description: Returns a Status representing success (identical to the default constructor).
requirements: None.

functions.name: mgos::Status::CANCELLED
functions.description: Returns a Status representing a cancelled operation. Exact code value is defined externally; message may be predefined or empty.
requirements: None.

functions.name: mgos::Status::UNIMPLEMENTED
functions.description: Returns a Status indicating the operation is unimplemented.
requirements: None.

functions.name: mgos::Status::UNKNOWN
functions.description: Returns a Status representing an unknown error condition.
requirements: None.

functions.name: mgos::Status::ok
functions.description: Returns true if the status is OK (code equals STATUS_OK).
requirements: The Status object must be initialized.

functions.name: mgos::Status::error_code
functions.description: Returns the integer error code carried by this Status.
requirements: The Status object must be initialized.

functions.name: mgos::Status::error_message
functions.description: Returns the error message string associated with this Status. For OK statuses, this is typically empty.
requirements: The Status object must be initialized.
The returned reference remains valid as long as the Status object remains alive and unmodified in ways that would replace its message.

functions.name: mgos::Status::operator==
functions.description: Equality operator. Returns true if both the error code and message match those of x.
requirements: Both this and x must be initialized Status objects.

functions.name: mgos::Status::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality operator. Logical negation of operator==.
requirements: Both this and x must be initialized Status objects.

functions.name: mgos::Status::ToString
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string representation of the Status, typically including the error code and message.
requirements: The Status object must be initialized.

functions.name: mgos::Errorf
functions.description: Creates and returns a Status from an error code and a printf-style formatted message. Use to build informative error statuses.
requirements: code may be any integer; specific meanings are defined externally (common/util/error_codes.h).
msg_fmt must be a valid, non-null C string specifying a printf-style format.
The variadic arguments must match the types and number of the format specifiers in msg_fmt (printf-like contract).

functions.name: mgos::Annotatef
functions.description: Returns a new Status based on another Status, with an additional printf-style formatted annotation message. Useful for adding context to an existing status.
requirements: other must be a valid Status reference.
msg_fmt must be a valid, non-null C string specifying a printf-style format.
The variadic arguments must match the types and number of the format specifiers in msg_fmt (printf-like contract).

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::StatusOr
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes the StatusOr in an error state with UNKNOWN status. Typically used to create a placeholder that will later be assigned a value or a specific status.
requirements: None beyond default-constructibility of T is not required for this constructor.
Object starts with status UNKNOWN; callers should check ok() before accessing value.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::StatusOr
functions.description: Constructs a StatusOr holding an error status. Passing an OK status is treated as a programming error and terminates the process via abort().
requirements: The provided status must not be OK; passing an OK status causes abort().
After construction, ok() will be false and no value is available.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::StatusOr
functions.description: Constructs a StatusOr from a value, indicating success. Intended usage: create a successful result that contains a copy of value. Note: The implementation provided does not explicitly set status_ to OK; behavior relies on Status’s default state and may be undefined if not OK—use with caution.
requirements: T must be copy-constructible.
Caller should only use ValueOrDie()/MoveValueOrDie() if ok() returns true; otherwise the program will abort.
Due to the header’s implementation, ensure status() is OK before accessing the value to avoid abort().

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::StatusOr
functions.description: Constructs a StatusOr from an rvalue value, moving it into the container to indicate success. Note: The implementation does not explicitly set status_ to OK; behavior depends on Status’s default state—verify ok() before access.
requirements: T must be move-constructible.
Caller should only use ValueOrDie()/MoveValueOrDie() if ok() returns true; otherwise the program will abort.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::StatusOr
functions.description: Copy constructor. Copies status and, if status is OK, copies the contained value from other.
requirements: T must be copy-constructible if other.ok() is true.
No additional preconditions for callers.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::StatusOr
functions.description: Move constructor. Copies the status and moves the contained value from other. Sets other’s status to UNKNOWN after the move.
requirements: T must be move-constructible if other.ok() is true.
After construction, other transitions to UNKNOWN status; do not assume its value is usable.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::operator=
functions.signature: template <typename T> const mgos::StatusOr<T> & mgos::StatusOr<T>::operator=(const mgos::StatusOr<T> &other)
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Copies status and, if status is OK, copies the contained value from other.
requirements: T must be copy-assignable if other.ok() is true.
Self-assignment is supported by the given implementation.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Moves status and, if status is OK, moves the contained value from other. Sets other’s status to UNKNOWN after assignment.
requirements: T must be move-assignable if other.ok() is true.
After assignment, other transitions to UNKNOWN status; do not assume its value is usable.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::operator=
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename U> const mgos::StatusOr<T> & mgos::StatusOr<T>::operator=(const mgos::StatusOr<U> &other)
functions.description: Conversion copy assignment operator. Copies status and, if status is OK, assigns the value converting from U to T via copy assignment.
requirements: T must be copy-assignable from U when other.ok() is true.
If other.ok() is false, only the status is copied; no value assignment occurs.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::operator=
functions.description: Conversion move assignment operator. Copies status and, if status is OK, move-assigns the value converting from U to T. Sets other’s status to UNKNOWN after assignment.
requirements: T must be move-assignable from U when other.ok() is true.
After assignment, other transitions to UNKNOWN status; its contained value should be considered moved-from and status UNKNOWN.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::status
functions.signature: template <typename T> const mgos::Status & mgos::StatusOr<T>::status() const
functions.description: Returns the contained Status object indicating success or the specific error. Use to check or inspect error details without accessing the value.
requirements: None. Safe to call at any time.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::ok
functions.description: Returns true if the StatusOr holds a successful result (status OK), false otherwise. Shorthand for status().ok().
requirements: None. Safe to call at any time.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::ValueOrDie
functions.signature: template <typename T> const T & mgos::StatusOr<T>::ValueOrDie() const
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the contained value if the status is OK; otherwise terminates the process via abort(). Intended for cases where failure is unrecoverable or has been checked earlier.
requirements: ok() must be true before calling; otherwise the function calls abort() and terminates the process.
The returned reference remains valid as long as the StatusOr object remains alive and unmodified.

functions.name: mgos::StatusOr::MoveValueOrDie
functions.description: Moves and returns the contained value if the status is OK; otherwise terminates the process via abort(). After a successful call, the object’s status becomes UNKNOWN and its previous value is moved-from.
requirements: ok() must be true before calling; otherwise the function calls abort() and terminates the process.
After calling, do not assume the StatusOr still contains a usable value; its status is set to UNKNOWN.

functions.name: json_walk
functions.signature: int json_walk(const char *json_string, int json_string_length, json_walk_callback_t callback, void *callback_data);
functions.description: Parses a JSON buffer and invokes a SAX-like callback for each token encountered. Use this for streaming-style processing without building a tree. Returns the number of processed bytes on success or a negative error code on failure.
requirements: json_string must point to a readable buffer of length json_string_length bytes containing JSON data.
json_string_length must be >= 0.
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with tokens and paths; callback_data is passed through and may be NULL.
Caller must handle negative return values as errors (e.g., JSON_STRING_INVALID or JSON_STRING_INCOMPLETE).

functions.name: json_printer_buf
functions.signature: int json_printer_buf(struct json_out *out, const char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Low-level printer that appends len bytes from str to an in-memory buffer described by out->u.buf. Intended to be used as json_out.printer when targeting a char buffer.
requirements: out must be initialized for buffered output (e.g., via JSON_OUT_BUF) with out->u.buf.buf pointing to writable memory and out->u.buf.size set to the total capacity.
str must be non-NULL if len > 0.
out must remain valid for the duration of the call; the buffer must not overlap invalid memory.
Caller should check the return value to know how many bytes were written (truncation may occur if capacity is insufficient).

functions.name: json_printer_file
functions.signature: int json_printer_file(struct json_out *out, const char *str, size_t len);
functions.description: Low-level printer that writes len bytes from str to a FILE* described by out. Intended to be used as json_out.printer when targeting a file stream.
requirements: out must be initialized for file output (e.g., via JSON_OUT_FILE) with a valid writable FILE* embedded in out.
str must be non-NULL if len > 0.
The FILE* must be open and writable for the duration of the call.
Caller should check the return value to know how many bytes were written.

functions.name: json_printf
functions.description: Formats and writes JSON-friendly output to the given json_out. Extends printf with specifiers for JSON types (%B, %Q, %.*Q, %V, %H, %M). Returns the number of bytes that would have been printed; if greater than the available buffer, overflow bytes are not written.
requirements: out must be initialized with a valid printer (e.g., JSON_OUT_BUF or JSON_OUT_FILE).
fmt must be a valid format string and must match the provided arguments.

For %B provide an int; for %Q provide const char* (nullable for null); for %.*Q provide int length followed by const char*; for %V provide const char* and int length; for %H provide int length then const char*; for %M provide a json_printf_callback_t and any arguments it expects.
Caller should check the return value to detect overflow (return value > actual bytes written implies truncation).

functions.name: json_vprintf
functions.signature: int json_vprintf(struct json_out *out, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of json_printf. Writes formatted JSON-friendly output to out using a pre-built va_list. Returns the number of bytes that would have been printed.
requirements: out must be initialized with a valid printer.
fmt must be non-NULL and match the arguments in ap.
ap must contain arguments matching the extended JSON specifiers as described for json_printf.
Caller should check the return value to detect overflow/truncation.

functions.name: json_fprintf
functions.description: Formats JSON-friendly output and writes it to the specified file. Creates the file if it does not exist and truncates it if it does. Returns the number of bytes printed, or a negative value on error.
requirements: file_name must be a non-NULL path to a file that can be created or opened for writing; process must have permissions.
fmt must be a valid format string and must match the provided arguments, including extended JSON specifiers (see json_printf).
Caller should handle negative return values as errors; on success, previous file contents (if any) are truncated.

functions.name: json_vfprintf
functions.signature: int json_vfprintf(const char *file_name, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of json_fprintf. Writes formatted JSON-friendly output to a file, creating or truncating it. Returns the number of bytes printed, or a negative value on error.
requirements: file_name must be a non-NULL path writable by the process.
fmt must be non-NULL and match arguments in ap, including extended JSON specifiers.
Caller should handle negative return values as errors; on success, file contents are replaced.

functions.name: json_asprintf
functions.description: Formats JSON-friendly output into a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string and returns it. Returns NULL on error. Caller owns and must free() the returned string.
requirements: fmt must be a valid format string and must match the provided arguments, including extended JSON specifiers.
Caller must free() the returned string when no longer needed.
On allocation failure, returns NULL; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: json_vasprintf
functions.description: va_list variant of json_asprintf. Returns a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string containing the formatted JSON-friendly output, or NULL on error. Caller must free() the result.
requirements: fmt must be non-NULL and match arguments in ap, including extended JSON specifiers.
Caller must free() the returned string.
Caller must check for NULL on allocation or formatting error.

functions.name: json_printf_array
functions.description: Helper %M callback for json_printf that prints a contiguous C array as JSON using an element format. Consumes from ap: void* array_ptr, size_t array_size, size_t elem_size, char* elem_fmt. Returns the number of bytes printed.
requirements: out must be initialized with a valid printer.

ap must point to a va_list that contains, in order: void* array_ptr, size_t array_size (in elements or bytes unknown; per comment it is the number of elements? The header states array_size, elem_size), size_t elem_size, char* fmt. Caller must supply these exactly as specified.
array_ptr must be non-NULL if array_size > 0 and must reference a contiguous memory block large enough for array_size elements of size elem_size.
elem_size must be > 0.
elem_fmt must be a valid format string for each element as expected by the printing routine.

functions.name: json_scanf
functions.signature: int json_scanf(const char *str, int str_len, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Scans a JSON buffer according to a scanf-like format with JSON extensions. Supports unquoted object keys and order-independent matching. Extended specifiers include %B, %Q, %V, %H, %M, %T. Returns the number of successfully scanned/converted elements, or a negative value on scan error.
requirements: str must point to a readable buffer of length str_len bytes containing JSON data.
str_len must be >= 0.
fmt must be a valid format string.
For %B, provide a pointer to int (or char if sizeof(bool)==sizeof(char)).
For %Q, provide a char**; the function mallocs a decoded string; caller must free() it on success.
For %V, provide a char** and int*; on success the data is base64-decoded, malloced, NUL-terminated, and length stored to the provided int*; caller must free() the char* result.
For %H, provide an int* (for output length) and a char** (for output buffer); on success hex is decoded, malloced, NUL-terminated; caller must free() the char* result.
For %M, provide a json_scanner_t function pointer followed by a void* user_data.
For %T, provide a struct json_token* which will be filled with the matched token.
Caller must check the return value: negative indicates a scan error; non-negative is the count of conversions performed.

functions.name: json_vscanf
functions.signature: int json_vscanf(const char *str, int str_len, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of json_scanf. Scans a JSON buffer according to a scanf-like JSON-aware format using a pre-built va_list. Returns the number of conversions performed, or a negative value on error.
requirements: str must point to a readable buffer of length str_len containing JSON data.
str_len must be >= 0.
fmt must be non-NULL and match the arguments in ap.
For each extended specifier, ap must supply pointers/values as detailed for json_scanf.
Caller must free any allocations produced for %Q, %V, and %H on success.

functions.name: json_scanf_array_elem
functions.signature: int json_scanf_array_elem(const char *s, int len, const char *path, int index, struct json_token *token);
functions.description: Finds an array element at the given JSON path and index within a JSON buffer and fills token with the matched element. Returns -1 if no such element is found; otherwise returns the element token length (non-negative).
requirements: s must point to a readable buffer of length len containing JSON data.
len must be >= 0.
path must be a valid JSON path string to an array location.
index should be >= 0; behavior for negative indices is unspecified.
token must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result.

functions.name: json_unescape
functions.signature: int json_unescape(const char *src, int slen, char *dst, int dlen);
functions.description: Unescapes a JSON-encoded string from src into dst. Buffers may overlap. If dst is too small (or zero-length), nothing is written but the required length is computed. Returns the length of the unescaped string in bytes.
requirements: src must point to a readable buffer of length slen containing a JSON-escaped string (without surrounding quotes).
slen must be >= 0.
dst may be NULL if dlen == 0; otherwise dst must point to a writable buffer of at least dlen bytes.
Caller should first call with dlen = 0 (and possibly dst = NULL) to get the required size, then allocate and call again to write output.

functions.name: json_escape
functions.signature: int json_escape(struct json_out *out, const char *str, size_t str_len);
functions.description: Escapes raw string bytes into a JSON-escaped representation and writes them to out. Returns the number of bytes printed.
requirements: out must be initialized with a valid printer.
If str_len > 0, str must be non-NULL and point to readable memory of at least str_len bytes.
Caller should check the return value to ensure the output was produced; for bounded buffers, may indicate truncation per the underlying printer semantics.

functions.name: json_fread
functions.description: Reads an entire file into a newly malloced buffer and returns it, or NULL on error. Caller must free() the returned buffer.
requirements: file_name must be a non-NULL path to a readable file.
Process must have permissions to open and read the file.
Caller must free() the returned buffer on success and check for NULL on error.

functions.name: json_setf
functions.signature: int json_setf(const char *s, int len, struct json_out *out, const char *json_path, const char *json_fmt, ...);
functions.description: Updates a JSON string by setting or deleting the value at json_path and writes the new JSON to out. If json_fmt is NULL, the key at path is deleted. If the path is missing, missing keys are added. An array path without an index (e.g., .a[]) appends to the array. Returns 1 if the string was changed, 0 otherwise.
requirements: s must point to a readable buffer of length len containing valid JSON.
len must be >= 0.
out must be initialized with a valid printer to receive the updated JSON.
json_path must be a valid path into the JSON document.
If json_fmt is non-NULL, the following varargs must match json_fmt following json_printf rules to produce the replacement value.
If json_fmt is NULL, the value at json_path will be deleted; caller should expect removal semantics.
Caller must check the return value to determine if an update occurred.

functions.name: json_vsetf
functions.signature: int json_vsetf(const char *s, int len, struct json_out *out, const char *json_path, const char *json_fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of json_setf. Applies an update or deletion at json_path in the given JSON source s and writes the result to out. Returns 1 if changed, 0 otherwise.
requirements: s must be valid JSON of length len.
len must be >= 0.
out must be initialized with a valid printer.
json_path must be a valid path into the JSON document.
If json_fmt is non-NULL, ap must contain arguments matching json_fmt per json_printf rules; if json_fmt is NULL, the key at path is deleted.
Caller must check the return value to detect whether a change occurred.

functions.name: json_prettify
functions.signature: int json_prettify(const char *s, int len, struct json_out *out);
functions.description: Pretty-prints a compact or minified JSON buffer into out with whitespace/indentation. Returns the number of processed bytes from the input buffer.
requirements: s must point to a readable buffer of length len containing JSON.
len must be >= 0.
out must be initialized with a valid printer to receive the prettified JSON.
Caller should use the return value to confirm how many input bytes were consumed/processed.

functions.name: json_prettify_file
functions.description: Pretty-prints the JSON content of the specified file in place. Returns the number of processed bytes on success, or a negative error code on failure. On error, the file content is not modified.
requirements: file_name must be a non-NULL path to a readable and writable file containing JSON.
Process must have permission to read and write the file.
Caller must handle negative return values as errors and may rely on the guarantee that on error the file is left unmodified.

functions.name: json_next_key
functions.signature: void *json_next_key(const char *s, int len, void *handle, const char *path, struct json_token *key, struct json_token *val);
functions.description: Iterates over object members at the given JSON path. On each call, fills key and val with the next property name and value token. Pass NULL as handle to begin; use the returned opaque handle for subsequent iterations. Returns NULL when iteration is complete.
requirements: s must point to a readable buffer of length len containing JSON.
len must be >= 0.
path must identify an object within the JSON document.
handle must be NULL to start iteration; thereafter, pass the previous return value until NULL is returned.
key and/or val may be NULL if the caller does not need them; if non-NULL, they must point to writable struct json_token storage.

functions.name: json_next_elem
functions.signature: void *json_next_elem(const char *s, int len, void *handle, const char *path, int *idx, struct json_token *val);
functions.description: Iterates over array elements at the given JSON path. On each call, fills idx with the current element index and val with the element token. Pass NULL as handle to begin; use the returned opaque handle for subsequent iterations. Returns NULL when iteration is complete.
requirements: s must point to a readable buffer of length len containing JSON.
len must be >= 0.
path must identify an array within the JSON document.
handle must be NULL to start iteration; thereafter, pass the previous return value until NULL is returned.
idx must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the element index.
val may be NULL if the caller does not need the value token; if non-NULL, it must point to writable struct json_token storage.

import os
import random
import struct
import zlib

# Data type: file data (arbitrary bytes)
# Target stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() that points to a file the fuzzer creates
# with the provided buffer as contents. Our job: generate interesting, but valid
# file contents. cs_read_file(path, &sz) simply reads entire file and appends a NUL.
# Thus any bytes are valid. We try to cover a range of interesting sizes/patterns:
# - empty file
# - small ASCII text with newline at end
# - binary blobs with zero bytes and 0xFF
# - repeating patterns and primes to tickle internal resizing loops
# - files around power-of-two thresholds (255, 256, 1023, 1024, etc.)
# - JSON-like text, base64, hex strings
# - random data with embedded NULs
# - data with CRC appended
# - long single line vs many small lines
# Ensure size <= 4096 bytes.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _ascii_text_block(rng: random.Random, n: int, newline=True) -> bytes:
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-.,:/\\\t"
    data = bytes(alphabet[rng.randrange(len(alphabet))] for _ in range(max(0, n - (1 if newline else 0))))
    if newline and n > 0:
        return data + b"\n"
    return data

def _repeating_pattern(pattern: bytes, total: int) -> bytes:
    if not pattern:
        return b""
    reps, rem = divmod(total, len(pattern))
    return pattern * reps + pattern[:rem]

def _json_like(rng: random.Random, approx: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce deterministic yet varied JSON-ish content
    keys = ["id", "name", "enabled", "values", "payload", "nested", "empty", "nullv"]
    rng.shuffle(keys)
    arr = [rng.randint(-1000, 1000) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10))]
    s = {
        keys[0]: rng.randrange(10**9),
        keys[1]: "str_" + str(rng.randrange(10**6)),
        keys[2]: bool(rng.getrandbits(1)),
        keys[3]: arr,
        keys[4]: "A" * rng.randrange(0, 64),
        keys[5]: {"k": "v", "n": rng.randrange(100)},
        keys[6]: "",
        keys[7]: None,
    }
    # Serialize simply to JSON-like without external deps
    def esc(t: str) -> str:
        return t.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"')
    parts = []
    parts.append('{')
    first = True
    for k, v in s.items():
        if not first:
            parts.append(',')
        first = False
        parts.append('"%s":' % esc(k))
        if isinstance(v, bool):
            parts.append('true' if v else 'false')
        elif v is None:
            parts.append('null')
        elif isinstance(v, int):
            parts.append(str(v))
        elif isinstance(v, str):
            parts.append('"%s"' % esc(v))
        elif isinstance(v, list):
            parts.append('[' + ','.join(str(x) for x in v) + ']')
        elif isinstance(v, dict):
            parts.append('{"k":"v","n":%d}' % v.get('n', 0))
        else:
            parts.append('null')
    parts.append('}')
    out = ''.join(parts).encode('utf-8')
    # Optionally pad or trim to approx
    if approx <= 0:
        return out
    if len(out) > approx:
        return out[:approx]
    return out + b"\n" + _ascii_text_block(rng, max(0, approx - len(out) - 1))

def _hex_string(rng: random.Random, nbytes: int) -> bytes:
    blob = _rand_bytes(rng, nbytes)
    return blob.hex().encode('ascii')

def _base64_like(rng: random.Random, nbytes: int) -> bytes:
    # simple base64 without padding correctness guarantees; for input variety only
    import base64
    blob = _rand_bytes(rng, nbytes)
    return base64.b64encode(blob)

def _with_crc(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    crc = zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return payload + b"\nCRC32:" + ("%08X" % crc).encode('ascii') + b"\n"

def _many_lines(rng: random.Random, target: int) -> bytes:
    lines = []
    cur = 0
    while cur < target:
        L = rng.randint(0, min(80, target - cur))
        line = _ascii_text_block(rng, L, newline=True)
        lines.append(line)
        cur += len(line)
    return b''.join(lines)[:target]

def _size_distribution(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias toward interesting boundaries
    choices = [
        0, 1, 2, 3,
        7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32,
        63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256,
        511, 512, 1023, 1024, 2047, 2048, 4095
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    # Otherwise pick a random size up to 4096
    return rng.randint(0, _MAX_SIZE)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    size = _size_distribution(rng)

    # Select a generator profile
    profiles = []
    profiles.append(lambda: b"")  # empty
    profiles.append(lambda: _ascii_text_block(rng, size, newline=True))
    profiles.append(lambda: _repeating_pattern(b"A", size))
    profiles.append(lambda: _repeating_pattern(b"\x00", size))
    profiles.append(lambda: _repeating_pattern(b"\xFF", size))
    profiles.append(lambda: _repeating_pattern(b"ABCDEF", size))
    profiles.append(lambda: _rand_bytes(rng, size))
    profiles.append(lambda: _json_like(rng, size))
    profiles.append(lambda: _hex_string(rng, max(0, size // 2)))  # hex grows 2x
    profiles.append(lambda: _base64_like(rng, max(0, int(size * 0.75))))
    profiles.append(lambda: _with_crc(_rand_bytes(rng, max(0, size - 15))))
    profiles.append(lambda: _many_lines(rng, size))
    profiles.append(lambda: (_repeating_pattern(struct.pack('<I', rng.getrandbits(32)), size)))

    # Mix sizes near thresholds by overriding size within profiles occasionally
    choice = rng.randrange(len(profiles))
    data = profiles[choice]()

    # Ensure upper bound
    if len(data) > _MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:_MAX_SIZE]

    return data

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# We need to feed two kinds of fuzz params in stubs:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): used as generic byte strings for json_printf args (%Q, %.*Q, %V, %H) and for cs_hex_decode source
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): used by json_fprintf as an output file path
# This generator returns a single bytes buffer which the harness will split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_* calls.
# Strategy:
# - Compose a sequence of segments prefixed with simple tags so the fuzzer infra (which usually slices)
#   will obtain diverse, valid substrings regardless of how it splits.
# - Include multiple JSON-safe and binary-safe strings, including valid hex strings with even/odd lengths,
#   base64-looking and arbitrary data, plus edge cases (empty, long, unicode, with NULs).
# - Include a plausible filename block with directories and various extensions.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

HEX_LOWER = "0123456789abcdef"
HEX_UPPER = "0123456789ABCDEF"
BASE64_CHARS = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/="
SAFE_FILENAME_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."


def _rand_hex(r: random.Random, length: int, upper: bool = False) -> str:
    alphabet = HEX_UPPER if upper else HEX_LOWER
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))


def _rand_base64ish(r: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    return "".join(r.choice(BASE64_CHARS) for _ in range(length))


def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some valid multi-byte UTF-8 code points.
    out: List[str] = []
    while len("".join(out).encode("utf-8")) < length:
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.7:
            out.append(r.choice(string.printable))
        elif t < 0.85:
            # Latin-1 supplement (2-byte)
            cp = r.randint(0x00A0, 0x00FF)
            out.append(chr(cp))
        elif t < 0.95:
            # Greek/Cyrillic (2-byte)
            cp = r.randint(0x0370, 0x052F)
            out.append(chr(cp))
        else:
            # Emoji range (mostly 4-byte)
            cp = r.choice([0x1F600, 0x1F602, 0x1F60D, 0x1F680, 0x1F4A9, 0x1F9E9])
            out.append(chr(cp))
    s = "".join(out)
    # Trim to requested byte length
    b = s.encode("utf-8")
    return b[:length].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")


def _rand_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce relative path to avoid permissions; include subdirs sometimes
    parts = []
    depth = r.randint(0, 2)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name_len = r.randint(1, 10)
        name = "".join(r.choice(SAFE_FILENAME_CHARS) for _ in range(name_len)).strip()
        if not name:
            name = "d"
        parts.append(name)
    # filename
    base_len = r.randint(1, 12)
    base = "".join(r.choice(SAFE_FILENAME_CHARS) for _ in range(base_len)).strip()
    if not base:
        base = "out"
    ext = r.choice([".json", ".txt", ".dat", ".log", ""]) if r.random() < 0.9 else ""
    fname = base + ext
    parts.append(fname)
    return "/".join(parts)


def _section(tag: str, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Simple tagged section: [TAG]\n<length decimal>\n<payload>\n
    header = f"[{tag}]\n{len(payload)}\n".encode("ascii")
    return header + payload + b"\n"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    blobs: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Hex strings for cs_hex_decode: include even and odd lengths, upper/lower, and mixed valid slices
    for _ in range(3):
        even_len = r.randint(0, 128) * 2  # even
        odd_len = even_len + 1 if even_len < 255 else 255
        lower_hex = _rand_hex(r, even_len, upper=False)
        upper_hex = _rand_hex(r, even_len, upper=True)
        mixed_hex = "".join(r.choice([c1, c2]) for c1, c2 in zip(lower_hex, upper_hex))
        odd_hex = _rand_hex(r, odd_len, upper=r.choice([True, False]))
        blobs.append(_section("HEX_EVEN_LOWER", lower_hex.encode("ascii")))
        blobs.append(_section("HEX_EVEN_MIXED", mixed_hex.encode("ascii")))
        blobs.append(_section("HEX_ODD", odd_hex.encode("ascii")))

    # 2) Non-hex data to trigger partial/invalid decode paths, but still reasonable
    for _ in range(2):
        base64ish = _rand_base64ish(r, r.randint(0, 200))
        ascii_mix = "".join(r.choice(string.printable) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 200)))
        blobs.append(_section("NONHEX_B64ISH", base64ish.encode("ascii")))
        blobs.append(_section("NONHEX_PRINT", ascii_mix.encode("latin1", errors="ignore")))

    # 3) JSON-related strings for %Q and %.*Q: include quotes, backslashes, unicode, and control chars
    json_strings: List[str] = []
    json_strings.append("")
    json_strings.append("simple")
    json_strings.append("with \"quotes\" and \\slashes\\ and\\nnewlines")
    json_strings.append(_rand_utf8(r, r.randint(0, 128)))
    json_strings.append("{" + ",".join(f"\"k{i}\":{i}" for i in range(r.randint(0,5))) + "}")
    for s in json_strings:
        blobs.append(_section("JSON_STR", s.encode("utf-8")))

    # 4) Binary payloads for %V (ptr,len) and %H (hex length then data): provide arbitrary and repetitive data
    for _ in range(3):

    # 5) Filenames for json_fprintf output
    for _ in range(3):
        fname = _rand_filename(r)

    long_hex = _rand_hex(r, r.randint(256, 1024), upper=r.choice([True, False]))

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary bytes
# Fuzzer uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(). We must return a single
# bytes buffer which the harness will split to feed those calls. We therefore
# construct a container format that encodes multiple concatenated blobs, each
# prefixed with a 2-byte length (little-endian), followed by that many bytes.
# This lets the harness obtain diverse, valid inputs deterministically.
#
# We generate several interesting byte sequences to exercise:
# - Empty
# - Small ASCII text
# - Binary with NULs
# - Repetitive patterns
# - Hex/Base64-like strings
# - JSON-like text for json_* functions
# - Random sizes up to 1024 each, while keeping total <= 4096 bytes
# Additionally, we include a small temp-friendly file content segment that a
# FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumer can write/read; the harness typically writes our
# buffer to files, so providing valid JSON and arbitrary bytes helps file-based
# printers and readers.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_SEG = 1024


def _le16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', n & 0xFFFF)


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = [
        *(ord('a') + i for i in range(26)),
        *(ord('A') + i for i in range(26)),
        *(ord('0') + i for i in range(10)),
        ord(' '), ord('_'), ord('-'), ord('/'), ord('.'), ord(','), ord(':'), ord('{'), ord('}'), ord('['), ord(']'), ord('"')
    ]
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int, pat: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not pat:
        return b"\x00" * n
    reps, rem = divmod(n, len(pat))
    base = pat * reps + pat[:rem]
    # Optionally inject a small mutation-free variation: rotate start
    if n > 0 and rng.random() < 0.3:
        k = rng.randrange(0, min(8, n))
        base = base[k:] + base[:k]
    return base


def _hex_string(rng: random.Random, n_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    data = rng.randbytes(n_bytes)
    return data.hex().encode('ascii')


def _base64ish(rng: random.Random, n_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce standard Base64 using Python for validity
    import base64
    raw = rng.randbytes(n_bytes)
    return base64.b64encode(raw)


def _json_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a small JSON object that exercises %B, %Q, %.*Q, %V (raw+len), %H (hex)
    bval = rng.randrange(0, 2)
    q = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randrange(0, 32)).decode('ascii', 'ignore')
    qn = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randrange(0, 32))
    v = rng.randbytes(rng.randrange(0, 24))
    h = rng.randbytes(rng.randrange(0, 24)).hex()
    # Represent v as base64 to be plausible for %V consumers
    import base64
    v64 = base64.b64encode(v).decode('ascii')
    obj = {
        "b": bool(bval),
        "q": q,
        "qn": qn.decode('ascii', 'ignore'),
        "v": v64,
        "h": h,
    }
    # Compact JSON without newlines
    import json
    return json.dumps(obj, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')


def _make_segments(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    segs: List[bytes] = []

    # Deterministic core cases
    segs.append(b"")  # empty
    segs.append(b"hello world")
    segs.append(b"\x00\x00\x00binary\x00data\xff\xfe")
    segs.append(_pattern_bytes(rng, 64, b"AB"))

    # Hex/Base64-like strings
    segs.append(_hex_string(rng, 16))
    segs.append(_base64ish(rng, 24))

    # JSON-like content
    segs.append(_json_like(rng))

    # Longer random ASCII and binary segments
    for _ in range(3):
        segs.append(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randrange(0, min(128, MAX_SEG))))
    for _ in range(3):
        segs.append(rng.randbytes(rng.randrange(0, min(256, MAX_SEG))))

    # Repetitive patterns to exercise ring buffers and CRC rolling behavior
    patterns = [b"\x00", b"\xff", b"\x01\x02\x03\x04", b"Lorem ipsum "]
    for pat in patterns:
        segs.append(_pattern_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(16, 160), pat))

    # A moderately sized buffer for CRC and append paths
    segs.append(rng.randbytes(rng.randrange(256, 768)))

    # A compact JSON array for json_printf_array-like usage
    arr = b"[" + b" ,".join(str(rng.randrange(0, 100)).encode('ascii') for _ in range(rng.randrange(0, 10))) + b"]"
    segs.append(arr)

    return segs


def _pack_segments(segs: List[bytes], rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Header: number of segments (1 byte, capped at 255)
    count = min(len(segs), 255)
    out.append(count)
    total = 1
    for i in range(count):
        s = segs[i]
        # Clip each segment to MAX_SEG and adjust to keep overall cap
        s = s[:MAX_SEG]
        # Ensure we never exceed MAX_TOTAL
        remaining = MAX_TOTAL - (total + 2)  # reserve for length field
        if remaining <= 0:
            # no room for this segment; write zero-length
            out += _le16(0)
            total += 2
            continue
        if len(s) > remaining:
            s = s[:remaining]
        out += _le16(len(s))
        out += s
        total += 2 + len(s)
        if total >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    # If we broke early, fix the count to actual number written
    actual = 0
    idx = 1
    while idx < len(out):
        if idx + 2 > len(out):
            break
        l = int.from_bytes(out[idx:idx+2], 'little')
        idx += 2 + l
        actual += 1
    out[0] = actual & 0xFF
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    segs = _make_segments(rng)
    # Shuffle to vary ordering per seed
    rng.shuffle(segs)
    buf = _pack_segments(segs, rng)
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: file path (NUL-terminated C string). Our fuzzer infra will place
# returned bytes as the initial content for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() source.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid, writable paths pointing to a file the process can open.
# - Cover variations: existing empty file, existing JSON content, non-existing
#   path (to exercise create/truncate), nested dirs, long names, special chars.
# - Keep under 4096 bytes.
# - Self-contained; no I/O here. We only emit the path bytes. The harness will
#   handle file creation if needed (stubs open with wb/wb+/reading elsewhere).
# Strategy:
# - Generate paths within the system temporary directory to maximize writability.
# - Mix existing-file-looking paths (simple filenames) and nested paths.
# - Include different extensions (.json, .txt, none) and special characters that
#   are valid on POSIX and commonly acceptable on Windows file names used here
#   (avoid reserved characters like \0, \n; avoid ':' except in drive spec on Windows).
# - Provide both absolute and relative paths.
# - Ensure NUL-terminated when consumed by C by simply returning bytes without
#   embedded NUL; the harness will treat as C-string by reading until NUL.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_@#%+.,! "+"[]{}()"

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid leading/trailing spaces only sometimes to test trimming edge, but keep valid
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid names that end with space or dot on Windows; trim those
    s = s.rstrip(' .')
    if not s:
        s = "f"
    return s

def _rand_extension(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    exts = ["", ".json", ".txt", ".bin", ".log", ".dat"]
    return rng.choice(exts)

def _rand_components(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    depth = rng.choices([0,1,2,3],[0.25,0.35,0.25,0.15])[0]
    comps = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        comps.append(_rand_filename(rng, 1, 8))
    leaf = _rand_filename(rng, 1, 24) + _rand_extension(rng)
    comps.append(leaf)
    return comps

def _maybe_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix absolute and relative prefixes. On Windows, avoid drive colon to keep portable.
    choices = ["relative", "abs_tmp", "dot", "dotdot"]
    kind = rng.choice(choices)
    if kind == "abs_tmp":
        return os.path.abspath(os.getenv("TMPDIR") or os.getenv("TEMP") or os.getenv("TMP") or "/tmp")
    elif kind == "dot":
        return "."
    elif kind == "dotdot":
        return ".."
    else:
        return ""  # relative bare filename

def _compose_path(prefix: str, components: List[str]) -> str:
    if prefix:
        path = prefix
        for c in components:
            path = os.path.join(path, c)
    else:
        path = os.path.join(*components)
    # Normalize to remove oddities (but keep filename content)
    return os.path.normpath(path)

def _make_variants(rng: random.Random, base_path: str) -> List[str]:
    variants = [base_path]
    # Add variant with long filename
    long_leaf = _rand_filename(rng, 20, 40) + _rand_extension(rng)
    variants.append(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(base_path) or ".", long_leaf))
    # Variant with nested dirs
    comps = _rand_components(rng)
    variants.append(_compose_path(os.path.dirname(base_path), comps))
    # Add path without extension
    variants.append(os.path.splitext(base_path)[0])
    # Add .json sibling
    variants.append(os.path.splitext(base_path)[0] + ".json")
    # Add hidden file on POSIX
    dirname = os.path.dirname(base_path) or "."
    variants.append(os.path.join(dirname, "." + _rand_filename(rng, 3, 12)))
    # Ensure uniqueness and reasonable length
    uniq = []
    seen = set()
    for v in variants:
        if len(v) > 4090:
            continue
        if v not in seen:
            seen.add(v)
            uniq.append(v)
    return uniq

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    prefix = _maybe_prefix(rng)
    comps = _rand_components(rng)
    base = _compose_path(prefix, comps)
    candidates = _make_variants(rng, base)
    # Choose one candidate biased towards JSON-friendly for json_prettify/json_fprintf
    weights = []
    for c in candidates:
        _, ext = os.path.splitext(c)
        if ext == ".json":
            w = 4.0
        elif ext in (".txt", ".log"):
            w = 2.0
        else:
            w = 1.0
        # Prefer temp dir absolute for writability
        if os.path.isabs(c) and (c.startswith("/tmp") or "\\\\" in c or \
                                 (os.getenv("TMP") and c.startswith(os.getenv("TMP")))):
            w *= 1.5
        weights.append(w)
    choice = rng.choices(candidates, weights=weights, k=1)[0]

    # Ensure the directory portion is not empty like '' for pure filename; keep as-is.
    # Return as UTF-8 bytes without embedded NUL; C side expects NUL-terminated.
    b = choice.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Guarantee size limit
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b

from typing import List

# We need to generate valid varint-encoded bytes for a single uint64 value,
# possibly followed by extra trailing bytes. The cs_varint_* format is a standard
# 7-bit per byte, little-endian base-128 with MSB as continuation bit.
# Encode function below implements that.

def _encode_varint_u64(x: int) -> bytes:
    if x < 0 or x > (1 << 64) - 1:
        raise ValueError("x out of uint64 range")
    out = bytearray()
    # Continuation style: write 7 bits per byte, LSB first; set MSB if more bytes follow
    while True:
        b = x & 0x7F
        x >>= 7
        if x:
            out.append(b | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

def _rand_u64(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias toward interesting edge cases while covering full range
    choices: List[int] = [
        0,
        1,
        127, 128, 129,
        16383, 16384, 16385,            # 2-byte boundary
        (1 << 21) - 1, (1 << 21), (1 << 21) + 1,  # 3-byte boundary
        (1 << 28) - 1, (1 << 28), (1 << 28) + 1,  # 4-byte boundary
        (1 << 35) - 1, (1 << 35), (1 << 35) + 1,  # 5-byte boundary
        (1 << 42) - 1, (1 << 42), (1 << 42) + 1,  # 6-byte boundary
        (1 << 49) - 1, (1 << 49), (1 << 49) + 1,  # 7-byte boundary
        (1 << 56) - 1, (1 << 56), (1 << 56) + 1,  # 8-byte boundary
        (1 << 63) - 1,
        (1 << 64) - 1,
    ]
    # With some probability choose from interesting set, otherwise random full-range
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return r.choice(choices)
    # Mix of small and large randoms
    mode = r.randrange(3)
    if mode == 0:
        return r.randrange(0, 1 << 14)  # small values fit in 1-2 bytes
    elif mode == 1:
        # random 64-bit value
        return (r.getrandbits(64))
    else:
        # construct value near a boundary 7*k bits
        k = r.randrange(1, 10)
        base = (1 << (7 * k)) - 1
        delta = r.randrange(-3, 4)
        val = base + delta
        if val < 0:
            val = 0
        if val > (1 << 64) - 1:
            val = (1 << 64) - 1
        return val

def _make_trailing_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    # Create deterministic-yet-random-looking trailing bytes using a mix of patterns
    patterns = []
    # Pattern 1: repeating short alphabet
    alpha = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
    if len(alpha) > 0:
        start = r.randrange(len(alpha))
        patterns.append((alpha[start:] + alpha[:start]) * ((n // len(alpha)) + 1))
    # Pattern 2: random bytes
    patterns.append(bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n)))
    # Pattern 3: incremental counter
    start = r.randrange(256)
    patterns.append(bytes((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(n)))
    buf = bytearray(n)
    src = patterns[r.randrange(len(patterns))]
    for i in range(n):
        buf[i] = src[i % len(src)]
    return bytes(buf)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a value and encode as varint
    val = _rand_u64(r)
    enc = _encode_varint_u64(val)

    # Optionally add extra trailing bytes (the fuzzer stub may provide provided size
    # shorter/equal/longer than the varint length). Keep extras small (<=10) as per stub.
    max_extra = 10
    extra_len = r.randrange(0, max_extra + 1)
    trailing = _make_trailing_bytes(r, extra_len)

    # Return the encoded varint followed by trailing bytes.
    out = enc + trailing
    # Ensure we do not exceed 4096 bytes (we won't, but be safe)
    return out[:4096]

# Generator for JSON-escaped string inputs (without surrounding quotes)
# Target fuzzer uses json_unescape(src, slen, ...), so we should produce
# valid escaped sequences as well as mixtures that exercise edge cases while
# remaining mostly valid.

_ESC_SIMPLE = {
    '"': '\\"',
    '\\': '\\\\',
    '/': '\\/',
    '\b': '\\b',
    '\f': '\\f',
    '\n': '\\n',
    '\r': '\\r',
    '\t': '\\t',
}

_HEX_DIGITS = '0123456789abcdefABCDEF'
_PRINTABLE = ''.join(ch for ch in (chr(i) for i in range(32, 127)) if ch not in '"\\')


def _rand_hex4(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(_HEX_DIGITS) for _ in range(4))


def _escape_char(c: str) -> str:
    # Escape a single character according to JSON rules
    if c in _ESC_SIMPLE:
        return _ESC_SIMPLE[c]
    o = ord(c)
    if o < 0x20:
        # Control chars must be escaped, prefer \uXXXX
        return '\\u%04x' % o
    if c == '"':
        return '\\"'
    if c == '\\':
        return '\\\\'
    # Safe to leave as-is
    return c


def _make_valid_sequence(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.35:
        # Plain chunk of unescaped safe characters
        length = rng.randint(1, 40)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(length))
    elif choice < 0.65:
        # Use simple escape sequences
        esc_keys = list(_ESC_SIMPLE.keys())
        # Generate a run of escapes mixed with safe chars
        parts: List[str] = []
        run = rng.randint(1, 10)
        for _ in range(run):
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                parts.append(_ESC_SIMPLE[rng.choice(esc_keys)])
            else:
                parts.append(rng.choice(_PRINTABLE))
        return ''.join(parts)
    else:
        # Unicode escapes: \uXXXX, including some interesting code points
        code_points = [
            0x0000, 0x0008, 0x0009, 0x000A, 0x000D,  # control chars
            0x002F, 0x005C, 0x0022,                 # '/', '\\', '"'
            0x007F, 0x00A0, 0x03A9, 0x0416, 0x20AC,  # DEL, NBSP, Ω, Ж, €
        ]
        parts: List[str] = []
        run = rng.randint(1, 6)
        for _ in range(run):
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                cp = rng.choice(code_points)
            else:
                cp = rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF)
            parts.append('\\u%04x' % (cp & 0xFFFF))
        return ''.join(parts)


def _make_edge_sequences(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Interesting but still valid or commonly accepted sequences for unescape
    seqs = []
    # Empty string
    seqs.append('')
    # Only escapes
    seqs.append('\\n\\r\\t')
    # Mixed escapes and text
    seqs.append('Hello\\nWorld\\t!')
    # Repeated backslashes that should fold correctly
    seqs.append('\\\\\\\\')  # two literal backslashes after unescape
    # Slashes with and without escaping
    seqs.append('path\\/to\\/file')
    # Boundary control chars via unicode
    seqs.append('\\u0000\\u0001\\u001f')
    # Quote and backslash
    seqs.append('He said: \\"Hi\\" \\\\\
')
    # Non-ASCII via \u
    seqs.append('Euro: \\u20AC Greek: \\u03A9 Cyrillic: \\u0416')
    # Large run of safe chars
    seqs.append(''.join('A' for _ in range(128)))
    # Long escaped unicode run
    seqs.append(''.join('\\u%04x' % rng.randint(0, 0x00FF) for _ in range(32)))
    return seqs


def _sized_join(parts: List[str], max_bytes: int) -> str:
    out = []
    size = 0
    for p in parts:
        if size + len(p) > max_bytes:
            # trim if needed
            remain = max_bytes - size
            if remain <= 0:
                break
            out.append(p[:remain])
            size += remain
            break
        out.append(p)
        size += len(p)
    return ''.join(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide a target total size up to 1024 bytes to keep below 4096 easily
    max_total = rng.randint(1, 1024)

    parts: List[str] = []

    # Start with some deterministic edge sequences
    edge = _make_edge_sequences(rng)
    rng.shuffle(edge)
    take = rng.randint(1, min(5, len(edge)))
    parts.extend(edge[:take])

    # Add a number of random valid sequences
    n_rand = rng.randint(3, 20)
    for _ in range(n_rand):
        parts.append(_make_valid_sequence(rng))

    # Occasionally embed explicitly escaped control chars from random ascii
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        ctrl_len = rng.randint(1, 16)
        ctrl = ''.join(_escape_char(chr(rng.randint(0, 31))) for _ in range(ctrl_len))
        parts.append(ctrl)

    # Occasionally add a block with every simple escape once
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(''.join(_ESC_SIMPLE[k] for k in _ESC_SIMPLE.keys()))

    # Join and cap length
    s = _sized_join(parts, max_total)

    # Ensure not empty (fuzzer may bail on trivial cases); if empty, add a simple escape
    if not s:
        s = '\\n'

    # Return as bytes; FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumes bytes as-is in its own harness
    return s.encode('utf-8')

# Data type: base64-encodable bytes used by %V in json_printf/json_fprintf
# The fuzz stubs fetch several strings:
#  - q: arbitrary string (used with %Q)
#  - qn: arbitrary string with explicit length (used with %.*Q)
#  - v: arbitrary bytes plus explicit length (used with %V, base64 encodable)
#  - h: hex string with explicit length (used with %H)
# They also request a filename (FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME) to write json_fprintf output.
# This generator returns a single bytes blob that the fuzzer will split to supply
# to those FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME calls. We therefore pack a small
# container format that yields valid and interesting values for q, qn, v, h, and
# a plausible writable filename path, while keeping each segment self-contained.
#
# Container layout (all little-endian):
#   magic: 4 bytes = b"JPF1"
#   b_flag: 1 byte (0 or 1) for %B
#   q_len: 2 bytes, then q bytes (UTF-8-ish printable)
#   qn_len: 2 bytes, then qn bytes (may include quotes and backslashes)
#   v_len: 2 bytes, then v bytes (arbitrary binary suitable for base64)
#   h_mode: 1 byte selector for hex content pattern
#   h_len: 2 bytes (even), then h bytes (hex ASCII 0-9a-fA-F)
#   fname_len: 2 bytes, then fname bytes (ASCII path-like)
#
# The fuzzer infra will provide these slices to the respective FUZZ_PARAM_*.
# We ensure: v is arbitrary bytes with provided length; h is valid hex text of even length;
# q and qn are bounded and include edge cases; filename is in a writable temp-y name style.

PRINTABLE = [c for c in (list(range(0x20, 0x7f))) if c not in ()]

HEX_DIGITS_LO = b"0123456789abcdef"
HEX_DIGITS_HI = b"0123456789ABCDEF"

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int, extra: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    # Bias towards typical JSON-safe chars plus occasionally quotes/backslashes
    base = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-./:@"
    pool = base + extra
    return bytes(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_jsony(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Include characters that exercise escaping when used with %Q and %.*Q
    extras = b"\"\\\b\f\n\r\t\x00\x01\x1f\x7f"
    data = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            data.append(rng.choice(extras))
        else:
            data.append(rng.choice(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-./:@[]{}:,+|*?"))
    return bytes(data)

def _rand_binary(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Arbitrary bytes to feed %V (base64). Include runs of zeros and high bytes.
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.2:
            # zero run
            run = min(n - i, rng.randint(1, 16))
            out.extend(b"\x00" * run)
            i += run
        elif choice < 0.4:
            # 0xff run
            run = min(n - i, rng.randint(1, 16))
            out.extend(b"\xff" * run)
            i += run
        else:
            # random bytes
            chunk = min(n - i, rng.randint(1, 32))
            out.extend(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(chunk))
            i += chunk
    return bytes(out[:n])

def _make_valid_hex(rng: random.Random, n_even: int, mode: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce exactly n_even ASCII hex chars (even). modes vary case/patterns.
    if n_even % 2 == 1:
        n_even += 1
    if n_even <= 0:
        return b""
    if mode == 0:
        # all lowercase
        digits = HEX_DIGITS_LO
    elif mode == 1:
        # all uppercase
        digits = HEX_DIGITS_HI
    elif mode == 2:
        # mix
        half = n_even // 2
        lo = bytes(rng.choice(HEX_DIGITS_LO) for _ in range(half))
        hi = bytes(rng.choice(HEX_DIGITS_HI) for _ in range(n_even - half))
        mixed = bytearray(lo + hi)
        rng.shuffle(mixed)
        return bytes(mixed)
    else:
        # patterned pairs to also decode to recognizable bytes (e.g., 00, 7f, ff, 41)
        pairs = [b"00", b"7f", b"FF", b"41", b"2a", b"0A", b"5a", b"10"]
        out = bytearray()
        while len(out) < n_even:
            p = rng.choice(pairs)
            out.extend(p)
        return bytes(out[:n_even])
    return bytes(rng.choice(digits) for _ in range(n_even))

def _make_filename(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a relative filename likely writable by the fuzzer environment.
    # Avoid directory traversal complexities but include subdirs sometimes.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3, 8)))
    name_core = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(4, 10))
    ext = rng.choice([b".json", b".txt", b".out", b".log", b".data"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else b""
    parts.append(name_core + ext)
    path = b"/".join(parts)
    if len(path) > max_len:
        path = path[:max_len]
    if len(path) == 0:
        path = b"out.json"
    return path

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide sizes with bias towards small and some interesting lengths for base64 and hex
    def pick_len(max_n: int, bias_zero: float = 0.15, bias_small: float = 0.6) -> int:
        if rng.random() < bias_zero:
            return 0
        if rng.random() < bias_small:
            return rng.randint(1, min(16, max_n))
        return rng.randint(17, max_n)

    # Upper bounds to stay under 4096 total
    q_len = pick_len(128)
    qn_len = pick_len(128)

    # For base64, lengths mod 3 matter; pick a mix
    v_base = pick_len(256)
    mod = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])
    v_len = v_base - (v_base % 3) + mod
    v_len = max(0, min(v_len, 512))

    # Hex must be even length
    h_len = pick_len(256)
    if h_len % 2 == 1:
        h_len += 1
    h_mode = rng.randrange(0, 4)

    b_flag = 1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0

    q = _rand_jsony(rng, q_len)
    qn = _rand_jsony(rng, qn_len)
    v = _rand_binary(rng, v_len)
    h = _make_valid_hex(rng, h_len, h_mode)
    fname = _make_filename(rng, 64)

    # Build container
    parts = []
    parts.append(b"JPF1")
    parts.append(struct.pack('<B', b_flag))

    parts.append(struct.pack('<H', len(q)))
    parts.append(q)

    parts.append(struct.pack('<H', len(qn)))
    parts.append(qn)

    parts.append(struct.pack('<H', len(v)))
    parts.append(v)

    parts.append(struct.pack('<B', h_mode))
    parts.append(struct.pack('<H', len(h)))
    parts.append(h)

    parts.append(struct.pack('<H', len(fname)))
    parts.append(fname)

    blob = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure size limit
    return blob[:MAX_TOTAL]
